items.title: Accordion
items.summary: Progressively reveal supporting information in place.
uses: FAQ sections where only one answer should be open at a time.
Settings or help pages that group long content under short, scannable questions.
avoids: Use expandable-card for a single standalone disclosure such as a plan or order summary.
Use tabs when sections are peer views that people switch between.

items.title: Account health
items.summary: A customer success card where a health score gauge, a renewal countdown and five sourced signals with sparklines lead into an AI risk summary and one recommended next step, like scheduling a QBR before usage slips further.
uses: A customer success or account page that needs a score, the signals behind it and a next step.
Renewal prep views where the countdown and risk drivers matter more than raw metrics.
avoids: Portfolio views across many accounts; use a table with a score column instead.
Deep metric exploration with axes and ranges; use a full chart.

items.title: Action button
items.summary: A compact button for frequent toolbar actions.
uses: A single async commit such as Save, Publish, or Submit where the result should appear on the button.
Call-to-action buttons where a trailing arrow invites the next step.
avoids: Use button with loading for plain form submits that do not need a success state.
Use action-swap when the control toggles between lasting states.

items.title: Action morph
items.summary: A floating button that morphs into a quick-action menu, then an inline form, then back with a check.
uses: Quick capture of tasks, notes, or comments without leaving the page.
Apps with a few frequent create actions that deserve a persistent button.
avoids: Use dialog or drawer for longer forms with several fields.
Use dropdown-menu when actions run immediately and need no input.

items.title: Action swap
items.summary: Swap an action label while preserving its place and intent.
uses: One control that cycles through related states, like Follow and Following or Send and Sent.
Toggles that run async work on press and should show a working phase and a failure message in place.
avoids: Use action-button for a single save or publish that ends in a success tick.
Use button when the label never changes state.

items.title: Activity feed
items.summary: A team activity feed grouped by day on a quiet avatar timeline, with a type filter, a live new updates button, expandable details, and a mark all read sweep.
uses: A workspace or project activity page for a team product.
A dashboard panel that shows what changed since someone last looked.
avoids: Use audit-log for compliance history that needs search, export, and exact timestamps.
Use notification-center for a personal inbox opened from a bell.

items.title: Activity heatmap
items.summary: See a year of activity at a glance, one square per day.
uses: Daily rhythm over a long range, like contributions or workouts.
Views where streaks and quiet weeks matter more than exact comparison.
avoids: Use bar-chart when the exact comparison is the point.
Use calendar to pick dates.

items.title: Activity rings
items.summary: Daily goals as tick rings that sweep, count up, and trace a second lap past 100%.
uses: Daily goals that fill up and can be exceeded, like move, exercise, and stand.
Fitness or habit dashboards with a week picker to compare days.
avoids: Use progress or gauge for a single value.
Use usage-meter for quotas and limits.

items.title: Activity terrain
items.summary: A 3D terrain of hourly activity you can orbit, zoom, fly into and flatten into a heatmap.
uses: Analytics or operations pages showing when a product is busiest across a week.
Showcase dashboards where a 3D view of a 7 by 24 grid adds impact, with a flat heatmap fallback.
avoids: Use activity-heatmap for a plain 2D grid that is easier to read.
Use bar-chart for totals by day or hour.

items.title: Agent approvals
items.summary: One approval card for agents: the waiting tool call reads like a permission prompt with the tool's mark, the agent's reason and its arguments, and you approve, deny or allow it from now on.
uses: Human in the loop control for agents that call tools with side effects: deploys, emails, database writes, payments and ticket changes.
An approvals card in an agent console or side panel where one person reviews, edits and decides tool calls quickly, from the keyboard if they like.
avoids: Use agent-run to follow one agent's steps and tool calls live, with an inline confirm inside the run.
Use mcp-servers to connect tools and set their permissions up front rather than per call.

items.title: Agent builder
items.summary: A card for setting up an AI agent: an inline editable name, a model picker, instructions, tool toggles with real app marks, and knowledge files with upload progress. A Configure / Test switch opens a compact chat that answers with the tools you turned on, and Publish ships the setup with a saved or unsaved state.
uses: Letting customers configure their own AI agent inside your product, like Intercom Fin, Zapier agents or an OpenAI GPT builder.
Internal admin screens where ops teams tune instructions, tools and knowledge for a support or billing agent.
avoids: Running or monitoring an agent in production: use agent-status or agent-routines.
Approving actions an agent wants to take: use agent-approvals.

items.title: Agent cursor
items.summary: A live document where Claude edits like a collaborator. Its labeled cursor comes out of its avatar, selects a paragraph and streams in a rewrite, adds a heading and fixes a typo, while a teammate's cursor reads along. Changes stay tinted until someone accepts or undoes them from a floating review bar.
uses: Showing an AI writing assistant that edits a doc alongside people, with accept and undo.
Landing or onboarding sections that demo a collaborative AI editor in motion.
avoids: Free form chat or Q&A: use a chat transcript component.
A real rich text editor: wire your editor's own collaboration cursors; this card renders read-only blocks.

items.title: Agent gallery
items.summary: A marketplace card of AI agent templates where you filter by team, search by agent or app, preview a sample run and install an agent inline: choose a workspace, grant access app by app, and the card confirms with a check.
uses: An agents or integrations page where people browse and install ready made AI agents.
Onboarding that suggests agent templates by team and installs one without leaving the page.
avoids: Configuring a single agent's prompt, tools or schedule: use a settings form or agent routines.
Showing a running agent's progress: use agent status or tool call.

items.title: Agent handoff
items.summary: A support conversation where an AI assistant hands off to a person. When it transfers, a card shows the summary it passes to the team and the typical wait. The person then joins and takes over, and a thin timeline on the left marks each step.
uses: A support widget where the AI answers first and escalates to a human agent.
Showing customers what the assistant shared with the team, so they do not repeat themselves.
avoids: A general chat with one assistant and no handoff: use chat-thread.
Showing an agent's internal steps or tool calls: use agent-timeline or tool-call.

items.title: Agent loop
items.summary: An illustration of the agent loop: gather context, take action, verify, repeat, with a bright head circling three stations around the model.
uses: Docs, explainers and landing pages that teach how an AI agent works: it gathers context, calls tools, checks the result and repeats until the task is done.
Showing why agents take several passes, with a failed check or a failed tool call that sends the loop round again.
avoids: Use agent-run or research-run to show a real agent's live steps and streamed output.
Use tool-call for a single tool call card inside a chat or a log.

items.title: Agent memory
items.summary: One card for what an assistant remembers about you: filter and search memories, edit or forget one in place, and turn saved memories and chat history on or off.
uses: Settings for an assistant that remembers people across chats, where people need to see, filter, search, correct and delete what it knows.
Showing the moment an assistant saves something from a chat, with a way to see where it was filed.
avoids: Use knowledge-base for documents and files an agent retrieves from, rather than short facts about the user.
Use context-window to show what fills a single conversation's token budget, rather than what persists across chats.

items.title: Agent orchestrator
items.summary: A lead agent splits a goal into a plan, fans the subtasks out to parallel worker lanes and merges what comes back, with each lane's model, progress and result in view.
uses: Showing a multi agent run where a lead model splits a task across subagents, such as research, audits, migrations or comparisons.
Debug or observability panels that need per worker progress, tool calls, errors, retries, tokens and cost in one view.
avoids: Use agent-run for a single agent working through steps in one thread.
Use agent-plan when the job is to review and edit a plan before anything runs.

items.title: Agent plan
items.summary: The plan an agent writes before it acts: edit, reorder or add steps while it is a draft, then watch it work through them as a live checklist.
uses: An agent should show and get approval for its plan before it edits code, runs commands or touches production.
A person needs to adjust the agent's plan (rename, reorder, remove or add steps) and then watch the same plan execute.
avoids: Use agent-run for a streaming transcript of everything the agent did, with tool calls and output, rather than a checklist of steps.
Use agent-approvals when the person approves individual risky actions one at a time instead of a whole plan up front.

items.title: Agent routines
items.summary: Scheduled agents in one card: each routine reads as a sentence with its schedule, next run countdown, connectors and destination, and opens smoothly to edit or run it now.
uses: Settings or automation screens where people schedule agents to run on their own and post results to Slack.
A card on a dashboard that shows at a glance which scheduled agents are healthy, which failed and when each runs next.
avoids: Use agent-run to watch a single agent work through a task in real time with its tool calls.
Use agent-tasks for a queue of one-off jobs that run once rather than on a schedule.

items.title: Agent run
items.summary: A single card that follows one AI coding agent through a task: steps stream in with the live one shimmering, tool calls open in place, and the agent stops on a two-file diff for you to approve or send back before it writes. When the run ends, the steps fold into one line and a result shows the files changed, the checks that passed and a pull request button.
uses: Coding agents and background jobs that read, search, edit and test, where people watch progress and approve the change before it is written.
Product surfaces that hand an agent a ticket and return a pull request, such as an issue tracker, a review tool or an IDE side panel.
avoids: Use research-run for a research agent that reads sources and writes a cited report.
Use agent-approvals for an inbox of pending approvals across many agents and tools.

items.title: Agent status
items.summary: A compact live status pill for a running AI agent: the agent's mark in a live ring, the current activity and an elapsed timer, opening into the steps so far.
uses: An app header, title bar or composer that needs to show at a glance that an agent is running, what it is doing and for how long.
Coding, research or browser agents that pause for approval, so the person can approve or deny without opening a full run view.
avoids: Use agent-run or research-run when the run itself is the page and every step, tool call and output needs room.
Use agent-approvals to review a queue of pending approvals across several agents.

items.title: Agent tasks
items.summary: A home for background coding agents: start a task on a repository and branch, watch each card move from queued to running to ready for review, and open a pull request from the result.
uses: A product surface where people hand coding tasks to background agents and come back later to review, open a pull request, retry or archive.
Dashboards for automated maintenance runs, such as dependency upgrades, flaky test fixes or codemods, where each run ends in a branch with a diff and checks.
avoids: Use agent-run to follow one live agent run in detail, with its plan, tool calls and output.
Use code-review when people need to read the diff line by line and leave comments; this block only summarizes the change.

items.title: Agent timeline
items.summary: A compact timeline of one orchestrated agent run: the orchestrator and its subagents share a time axis, handoffs draw in between rows, and a playhead replays thinking, tool calls and waiting while the header counts time, tokens and cost. Hover a span for what it did, or click it to trace its handoff path.
uses: Showing how an orchestrator split work across subagents and how long each part took, in a run history, a trace viewer or a debugging panel.
Replaying a finished agent run in a product demo or changelog, with real numbers for time, tokens and cost.
avoids: Use agent-orchestrator for a full screen of agent lanes with streaming text and messages; this timeline is the compact, reusable view of timing.
Use observability-trace for distributed request tracing across services rather than agents.

items.title: AI answer
items.summary: One AI answer set like a clean article: it thinks, shows its sources as small cards with colored marks, and streams a formatted answer where every citation lights the sentence it supports. Copy, regenerate with options, rate, share, page through versions and ask a related question in place.
uses: An answer page where one question gets one well formatted, cited answer that people read, copy and share.
Docs and help center assistants that must show where each claim comes from.
avoids: Use ai-chat for a back and forth conversation with many turns kept on screen.
Use research-run for long multi step research that plans searches and reads many sources before writing.

items.title: AI chat
items.summary: A full-screen AI chat where answers stream in as markdown with folding reasoning, tool chips and cited sources. People can switch chats and models, edit or retry a message into versions, rate replies and stop a reply mid-stream.
uses: A multi turn assistant inside a product page, drawer or dashboard card, with streaming answers, reasoning, tools and citations.
Any place users need to retry, edit, rate or copy answers and switch models mid conversation.
avoids: Use ai-composer when you only need the prompt box with attachments, mentions and commands.
Use ai-answer for a single question and a long, article like answer with sources.

items.title: AI command
items.summary: A Cmd+K command palette with an AI mode. Search pages and actions, or press Tab to ask a question: the answer streams inside the palette with numbered sources, and the next steps it suggests, like filing a Linear issue or opening a Notion doc, run straight from the list.
uses: A global Cmd+K in a SaaS app where people both jump to pages and ask questions about their workspace.
Search that should fall back to an AI answer when nothing matches.
avoids: A long, multi-turn conversation: use a chat thread.
Plain navigation with no AI: use command-palette.

items.title: AI composer
items.summary: The prompt box at the bottom of an AI app: files upload in place, / opens commands, @ inserts mentions, a model and effort menu sits in the toolbar, and the send button turns into a stop control ringed by the reply's progress.
uses: The prompt box of an assistant, a coding agent or an in-product AI feature where people attach files, mention docs and pick a model.
A new chat screen that should open on a greeting and suggestions, then show the first exchange.
avoids: Use ai-chat for a full conversation with history, message actions and a sidebar of chats.
Use ai-inline-edit to rewrite a selection inside a document instead of chatting about it.

items.title: AI feature launch
items.summary: An in-product launch card for an AI feature. A looping mini demo plays above a three-step tour (inline rewrite, thread summary, ask your workspace), with benefit rows, an admin-gated "Enable for my workspace" switch, and Try it now and Learn more actions.
uses: Announcing a new AI feature inside the product, with a tour of what it does and a switch to turn it on for the workspace.
Admin-gated rollouts where an admin enables AI for everyone and members can still try it.
avoids: Multi-step configuration with real inputs (models, data sources): use ai-setup-wizard.
Ongoing activation tasks: use onboarding-checklist.

items.title: AI inline edit
items.summary: A document you edit with AI in place: ⌘K on a selection, watch the rewrite stream in as a diff, accept each change, and Tab through ghost text.
uses: Rewriting a selection: shorten, clarify, change tone or fix grammar in place.
Inline autocomplete while writing documents or messages.
avoids: Rich formatting such as headings, lists or links; the block edits plain paragraphs.
Asking questions about a page; use ai-side-panel.

items.title: AI insight card
items.summary: A KPI card that explains itself. Explain streams a short reason for the change and ranks three drivers with contribution bars. A numbered annotation lights up on the sparkline as each driver is read, and follow-up chips ask the next question in place.
uses: A dashboard KPI where readers ask why it moved, such as net revenue, MRR, signups or churn.
Weekly business reviews and finance dashboards that want an explanation next to the number.
avoids: Open ended questions across many tables: use ask-your-data.
A plain number with no explanation: use metric-card or stat-card.

items.title: AI mascot
items.summary: A small assistant character, a soft pebble with pill eyes and a companion dot, that shows what the AI is doing. It breathes and glances when idle, leans in to listen, looks up while the dot orbits its head, reads along the line it writes, squints with a sparkle when done and shakes once with worried brows on an error.
uses: Give an assistant a face that shows what it is doing: in a reply header, beside a composer, on an image canvas while it generates, or in an empty state.
Products that want generation to feel alive and friendly without a spinner, with states that read at 24px.
avoids: Use agent-status when people need the steps, tools and elapsed time of a run, not just a mood.
Use text-shimmer alone for a plain "Thinking" line in dense interfaces where a character would distract.

items.title: AI search bar
items.summary: A search card for an app or docs, where typing lists grouped results right away (Docs, Customers, Issues) and pressing Tab streams a short AI answer on top. The answer's numbered citations point to the results below it.
uses: A product or docs search where people mix finding a page or record with asking a question.
Support and success tools that search docs, customers and tickets in one place.
avoids: Use ai-answer for a full answer page with long formatted answers, follow ups and feedback.
Use ai-chat for a back and forth conversation.

items.title: AI setup wizard
items.summary: A three-step setup card for turning on an AI feature. You connect Notion, Google Drive, Confluence or Zendesk and watch each one sync. Then you pick the model, tone and guardrails, and ask a test question whose answer streams with numbered citations before you go live.
uses: Turning on an AI answers feature for a support, sales or internal knowledge team, like Intercom Fin, Zendesk AI or Notion Q&A.
Onboarding admins to a copilot that needs data sources, a model choice and guardrails before it is enabled.
avoids: Configuring an agent's instructions, tools and files in depth: use agent-builder.
Only choosing a model: use model-picker.

items.title: AI side panel
items.summary: An assistant docked beside a page that reads it and edits it: ask about the page or a selected passage, review each edit as a word diff, and apply it with a tint sweep on the page and one-click undo.
uses: An assistant next to a document or record that can summarize it and propose edits.
Copilot style help where edits must be approved, applied visibly and undone.
avoids: A standalone conversation; use ai-chat.
Rewriting a passage in place with no side panel; use ai-inline-edit.

items.title: AI spark
items.summary: A brand-quality animated spark mark. Four tapered rays and four lighter diagonals breathe at rest, ripple while thinking, pulse like a heartbeat while writing, then gather and settle when done. Every status change blends from the pose the mark is already in.
uses: Showing that an assistant is thinking or writing, inline above a streaming reply.
A send or generate button that turns into a working indicator inside a composer.
avoids: Determinate progress with a known percentage; use a progress bar or the generation stats component instead.
Multi step agent runs where each step needs its own state and detail; use agent-status or agent-run.

items.title: AI translate
items.summary: A message card where picking a language streams the AI translation in place, sentence by sentence over the dimmed original, with a detected-language chip, a Show original toggle and a status line credited to the model's mark.
uses: Messages, comments, reviews or support tickets written in another language, translated on demand inside the product.
Release notes or announcements that readers in several regions open in their own language.
avoids: Translating a whole page or app interface; use your i18n framework.
Long documents with headings and lists; this renders one plain paragraph.

items.title: AI workflow
items.summary: A Linear-style AI workflow card where a Gmail trigger, a Claude step, a branch and Slack and Linear actions sit on one hairline rail, and a test run glides down it, opening each step's output inline. Steps are added from a compact command menu with real app marks.
uses: An automation or integrations page where people assemble a short trigger, AI step and action flow and want to test it in place.
Onboarding or marketing surfaces that show how an AI step slots between real apps, with a working test run.
avoids: Large free-form graphs with many branches, loops or merges: use a canvas editor instead.
Showing a single tool call or a live agent's steps: use tool-call or agent-run.

items.title: Alert
items.summary: A persistent message that helps people recover or continue.
uses: Persistent, in-flow messages about a page or form, such as an expiring card.
Status that changes over time, where one alert should morph between tones.
avoids: Use toast or toast-stack for transient results of an action.
Use empty-state when there is no content to show.

items.title: Animated counter
items.summary: Give changing totals a clear sense of movement.
uses: Standalone numbers that change, such as totals, prices, or live counts.
Hero stats that roll up from zero when they scroll into view, via animateOnView.
avoids: Use metric-card or stat-card when the number needs a card around it.
Use text-morph for words rather than numbers.

items.title: Announcement bar
items.summary: A top banner that rotates messages, counts down, and collapses smoothly when dismissed.
uses: Site-wide promotions, launches, or maintenance notices at the top of every page.
Rotating two to four short announcements in one slim bar.
avoids: Use alert for a message tied to one section or form.
Use toast for feedback on something the visitor just did.

items.title: API keys
items.summary: API key management where Create key unfolds into its form and each secret is shown once.
uses: The developer settings page of an API product.
Key management with scopes, environments, and a one-time secret reveal.
avoids: Use webhooks for event endpoints and signing secrets.
Use integrations for OAuth connections to other apps.

items.title: Arc foundation
items.summary: Arc design tokens (color, surface, radius, shadow, accent, focus, light and dark themes), plus the shared motion presets. Install once per app.

items.title: Arc motion tokens
items.summary: The shared motion presets (durations, easings, springs, staggers) Arc components import. Installed automatically with any item that uses them.

items.title: Arc agent skill
items.summary: An Agent Skill that teaches Claude Code and other agents how to choose, install, and compose Arc components, with rule files for design, components, motion, accessibility, composition, and responsive layout.

items.title: Ask your data
items.summary: A natural language to chart card: you ask a question, PostgreSQL streams into a collapsible, syntax highlighted panel, the query runs with a rolling row count, and the answer builds as stacked bars, lines or a table, with a one line insight streamed in underneath.
uses: Letting people ask product or business questions in plain words and see a chart, with the SQL one click away to verify or copy.
Embedding an analytics answer in a dashboard card, an admin page or an AI assistant's result view.
avoids: Use bar-chart or line-chart when the query is fixed and there is no question to ask.
Use tool-call to show a database query as one step inside a longer agent transcript.

items.title: Availability picker
items.summary: Find a meeting time across people and see the choice come together.
uses: Picking a meeting time that works for several attendees.
Booking flows that show a few days and open slots with a confirmation step.
avoids: Use calendar or date-picker to pick a single date.
Use time-picker for a free time input.

items.title: Avatar
items.summary: A compact identity marker for people and accounts.
uses: Showing one person next to their name, comment, or record.
Presence in a header or list, via the online or offline status dot.
avoids: Use avatar-group for several people with an overflow count.
Use user-menu when the avatar is the trigger for account actions.

items.title: Avatar group
items.summary: Show a team or set of contributors in a small space.
uses: Showing who owns or edits something in a header, card, or table cell.
Collaborator stacks where people join and leave while the page is open.
avoids: Use avatar for a single person.
Use a list or sortable-data-table when people need to see every name and role.

items.title: Avatar upload
items.summary: Click or drop a photo onto the avatar to crop it in place with drag, pinch and zoom. It uploads through a progress ring and settles, with clear errors and retry.
uses: Profile, account and team member settings where a person sets their own photo.
Workspace or organization logos that display in a circle.
avoids: Several files or documents at once: use file-dropzone.
Free form crops with aspect ratios, rotation or a large canvas: use image-cropper.

items.title: Badge
items.summary: A small label for status, category, or metadata.
uses: Short statuses next to titles or in table cells, such as Live, Draft, or Failed.
Counts or states that change in place and should morph instead of jump.
avoids: Use alert or toast when the message needs a full sentence.
Use chip-group when people toggle the values.

items.title: Bar chart
items.summary: Compare one measure across days and scrub any bar for its value.
uses: One measure across days, weeks, or months, with an average line.
Charts with a range switch, where stable keys let bars morph between ranges.
avoids: Use sparkline for a compact trend.
Use activity-heatmap for daily rhythm over a year.

items.title: Billing overview
items.summary: A billing page where the plan card morphs into a picker and usage, invoices, and card follow.
uses: The billing settings page of a SaaS app.
Pages that show plan, usage, payment method, and invoices together.
avoids: Use plan-comparison or usage-pricing on a public pricing page.
Use cancel-flow for the cancellation journey.

items.title: Billing toggle
items.summary: A monthly and yearly switch with a savings badge and prices that roll to the new amount.
uses: The billing period switch at the top of a pricing page.
Any price display that should roll to a new amount when a period or plan changes, using BillingPrice.
avoids: Use segmented-control for switching views or filters with no pricing meaning.
Use radio-group when options need descriptions or a vertical layout.

items.title: Black hole
items.summary: A delete transition that pulls the chosen items into a tiny singularity while the rest of the list bends around it; undo spins them back out.
uses: Deleting or archiving a handful of selected rows, cards, or files, with an Undo right after.
Emptying a trash, clearing notifications, or dismissing a batch where the removal should feel final.
avoids: High frequency deletes such as clearing a single chip or tag. Use a quick height collapse instead.
Irreversible actions without undo. The spectacle should not stand in for a confirmation.

items.title: Blog grid
items.summary: A blog index with a featured post, category filter, post cards, pagination and an in-place reader.
uses: A marketing site blog or journal index.
Resource hubs with a few categories and a featured story.
avoids: Use changelog-page for release notes with versions.
Use a data table for large archives that need sorting and search.

items.title: Booking pill
items.summary: One pill that reshapes through party size, date, time, and a ticket.
uses: Venue or service pages where booking a table or slot is the one action people came for.
Mobile-first flows that walk through party size, date, time, and confirm in one surface.
avoids: Use date-picker and time-picker inside a regular form for multi-field checkouts.
Use stepper or multi-step-form for longer flows with many fields.

items.title: Bottom sheet
items.summary: A sheet that rests at a peek or full height and follows your finger.
uses: Mobile-first secondary tasks such as details, filters, or share options.
Content that benefits from a peek height before expanding to nearly full screen.
avoids: Use dialog for interrupting decisions on any screen size.
Use drawer for side panels on wide desktop layouts.

items.title: Branch graph
items.summary: A git commit graph where branches draw in as colored lanes, merge commits join lines, a rebase lifts commits and replays them onto main, a squash folds them into one, and hovering a commit shows its message, author and diff stats.
uses: A merge strategy picker in a code review or pull request screen, showing exactly what main will look like afterwards.
A commit history panel in a developer tool, with hover details and keyboard browsing.
avoids: Use git-branches for a looping, non-interactive illustration of a branch, pull request, and release.
Use a timeline or changelog for releases people need to read rather than a commit graph.

items.title: Breadcrumb
items.summary: Show where a page sits in a hierarchy.
uses: Showing where a page sits in a hierarchy, such as Workspace, Settings, Billing.
Client-side paths like a file browser, where crumbs call onClick instead of navigating.
avoids: Use tree-view when people need to browse the whole hierarchy.
Use tabs for switching between sibling views.

items.title: Brush chart
items.summary: A dense time series with an overview strip: drag a window to zoom, resize it by its handles, and read events in place.
uses: Product analytics with a year or more of daily data.
Incident reviews where events need to be read against a metric.
avoids: Use line-chart for a few weeks of data or several series.
Use sparkline for a small inline trend without interaction.

items.title: Budget variance
items.summary: Budget against actual operating spend by department as aligned bullet charts, with favorable and unfavorable variance, a month, quarter and year to date switch that springs every bar, in-place drill-down into budget lines, and a total row.
uses: Monthly close and budget review screens that compare planned and actual operating spend by department or cost center.
Finance dashboards where a controller needs to see at a glance which teams are over, which are under, and by how much.
avoids: Use mrr-waterfall to explain how a single total moved from one value to another.
Use usage-forecast to project spend against a cap over time.

items.title: Button
items.summary: A clear, responsive action with quiet secondary states.
uses: Any single action on a page, form, or dialog, such as Save, Continue, or Cancel.
Actions whose label changes in place, like Save to Saved, where the width should spring instead of jump.
avoids: Use action-button when the button itself should show pending and success states after an async commit.
Use split-button when one default action has two to five close variants.

items.title: Button group
items.summary: Related actions joined into one surface with hairline dividers: a hover highlight glides between segments, the pressed one answers in place, and an attached menu can close the row.
uses: A small set of related actions on the same object, shown together in a header, toolbar or card footer.
Compact tool clusters such as zoom out, the current level and zoom in, or stacked map controls.
avoids: Use toggle-group or segmented-control when the segments are options that stay selected.
Use split-button when there is one main action and a few variants of it.

items.title: Calendar

Picking one date with blocked days via minDate, maxDate, and disabledDates.

Use time-picker for times of day.

items.title: Call insights

A call review queue for sales managers who coach on talk time and objection handling.

An internal meeting recap without a prospect or deal: use meeting-summary.

items.title: Cancel flow

Flows that offer a discount, pause, or downgrade before confirming the cancel.
avoids: Use dialog with hold-to-confirm for a one step destructive action without offers.
Use plan-comparison when people are choosing a plan rather than leaving.

items.title: Card
items.summary: A contained group of related content and actions.
uses: Browsable items in a grid, such as projects, listings, or posts.
Items that should open into a larger quick look dialog without leaving the page, via details.
avoids: Use expandable-card for inline disclosure without a dialog.
Use stat-card or metric-card for numbers.

items.title: Card stack
items.summary: Review a deck one card at a time, with a throw and an undo.
uses: One-by-one triage such as shortlisting, review queues, or onboarding picks.
Decks where swiping left or right should be undoable.
avoids: Use a list or sortable-data-table when people compare items side by side.
Use carousel to browse items without deciding.

items.title: Card to article
items.summary: Story cards that open into full articles with one seamless morph and shrink back into their exact slot when dragged down.
uses: Blogs, journals, and changelogs where each entry has a strong image.
Case study and portfolio grids.
avoids: Use a normal link to a page when articles are long or need their own URL and SEO.
Use expandable-card for small inline details.

items.title: Carousel
items.summary: Browse a row of slides by dragging, flicking, or arrowing through them.
uses: A short set of peer items where neighbouring slides hint at more.
Galleries browsed by drag, flick, trackpad swipe, or keys.
avoids: Use cover-flow for a showpiece gallery and photo-grid to show everything at once.
Use card-stack for deciding on items one at a time.

items.title: Cart drawer

Stores that show a free shipping threshold and promo codes before checkout.

Use checkout-summary when you only need the order summary and totals.

items.title: Catch up
items.summary: A catch me up digest for when you return, where one button reads Slack, Linear, GitHub and Gmail for the range you pick and streams back a short ranked summary: Needs you, Decisions made, Shipped and FYI. uses: A home or inbox screen that summarizes what happened across connected tools while the user was away.
An AI assistant feature that turns hundreds of notifications into a short ranked list with jump links.
avoids: A live notification feed where every event matters; use a plain activity list instead.
A long-form report or meeting summary with paragraphs; use a document view or ai-chat.

items.title: Changelog feed
items.summary: Release notes you can filter, open in place, and scroll through month by month.
uses: A product changelog or release notes page grouped by month.
Release notes with type filters such as features, fixes, and improvements.
avoids: Use timeline for a short vertical list of events without filters.
Use accordion for plain expandable content that is not dated.

items.title: Charge session
items.summary: An EV or device charging card. Energy packets flow from a charger along the cable into the battery pack, which fills toward a draggable charge limit. The charge curve tapers near full, and power, energy, time to limit and cost update live. Stop charging drains the flow.
uses: An EV or fleet app that shows a live charging session with a charge limit.
A charge point operator console where staff watch power, energy and cost for one bay.
avoids: Use usage-meter or progress for a static quota or a simple percentage.
Use gauge for a single live reading without a session, curve or cost.

items.title: Chat thread
items.summary: A chat thread with grouped messages, reactions, read receipts, typing, and a composer with attachments.
uses: Customer support or in-app messaging with read receipts and typing state.
Team or DM threads that need reactions and image or file attachments.
avoids: Use log-stream for streaming system or build output.
Use timeline for an activity history rather than a two-way conversation.

items.title: Checkbox
items.summary: A binary choice with a precise, legible state.
uses: Independent on and off choices confirmed by a submit, such as accepting terms.
Parent rows that show a partial selection through the indeterminate state.
avoids: Use switch for settings that apply immediately.
Use radio-group when only one option can be chosen.

items.title: Live checkout
items.summary: A subscription checkout whose summary recomputes as you edit, then glides to the centre and unfolds into a receipt.
uses: Upgrade from a free plan to a paid team plan.
Paid signup where seats and add-ons change the price.
avoids: A physical goods cart with shipping; use checkout-flow.
Only showing totals without payment; use checkout-summary.

items.title: Checkout summary
items.summary: An order summary with a promo code that becomes a chip, discount and tax lines, and pay button states.
uses: The last step before a hosted checkout such as a Stripe session redirect.
A single product purchase with launch discounts or promo codes.
avoids: Use checkout-flow when you collect shipping and card details in the page.
Use cart-drawer for a cart with several items and quantities.

items.title: Chip group
items.summary: Filter by a few facets with chips that morph as you pick them.
uses: Facet filters people toggle often, like topics or categories.
Single clearable choices shown as chips, via multiple={false}.
avoids: Use multi-select when space is tight.
Use checkbox in forms.

items.title: Choropleth explorer
items.summary: A filled-region map that shades every state or region by revenue, growth or penetration on a stepped scale, with a country switch (United States, Canada, Brazil, United Kingdom, France, Germany, Italy, Australia), a hoverable legend, a synced ranked list and a camera zoom into local detail.
uses: Sales, revenue or usage dashboards that break a metric down by state, country or territory.
Market coverage and penetration reviews where a region's own subareas explain its number.
avoids: Use offices-map to place pins at specific locations such as offices or stores.
Use revenue-globe for flows and totals on a spinning globe when geography is ambience rather than the comparison.

items.title: Code block
items.summary: Present code with legible hierarchy and copy access.
uses: Documentation snippets and install commands with a copy button.
Long files that should collapse to a few lines with Show all, via maxLines.
avoids: Use copy-button alone for a one-line value such as an API key.
Use text-stream for code arriving from an AI response in progress.

items.title: Code suggestion
items.summary: An AI code edit suggestion where the model's proposed changes stream into a small editor panel as inline diff hunks, and you accept or reject each one, or all at once with Cmd+Enter. Accepted hunks fold into the file with a smooth height change.
uses: Showing an AI's proposed edit to a file as an inline diff the person accepts or rejects hunk by hunk.
Approving an agent's file change before it is written, with a clear record of what was kept.
avoids: Use a dedicated diff tool for large multi file diffs or side by side comparisons; this card is for one file and a handful of hunks.
Use code-magic-move to animate code from one version to another without a review step.

items.title: Cohort retention
items.summary: A cohort retention triangle that morphs into retention curves and rewashes by segment.
uses: Growth or customer success dashboards comparing how signup cohorts retain month over month.
Views that need both the cohort triangle and retention curves from the same data.
avoids: Use journey-flow for paths between funnel steps.
Use activity-heatmap for activity by day rather than by cohort.

items.title: Color picker
items.summary: A swatch that grows into a picker with format morphing, eyedropper, saved swatches, and contrast readout.
uses: Theme editors and brand settings where users choose an exact color.
Design tools that need hex, RGB, HSL, and OKLCH input plus opacity.
avoids: Use segmented-control or radio-group when the choice is between a few fixed colors.
Use input for a plain hex field with no visual picking.

items.title: Combobox
items.summary: Search and select from a list without leaving the field.
uses: Single-choice fields with long lists, such as time zones or countries.
Lists where people know the name and want to type, including aliases via keywords.
avoids: Use select for a short list where typing adds nothing.
Use multi-select when several values can be chosen.

items.title: Command palette
items.summary: A complete keyboard driven action surface with search, grouped results, and shortcuts.
uses: App-wide command search opened with Cmd or Ctrl plus K.
Jumping to pages, creating items, and running actions from one input.
avoids: Use combobox to pick a value inside a form.
Use dropdown-menu for a short list of actions.

items.title: Comment thread
items.summary: Threaded comments with replies, reactions, mentions, inline edit, and resolve.
uses: Review threads on documents, designs, tickets, or pull requests.
Discussions that need replies, reactions, mentions, and a resolved state.
avoids: Use chat-thread for real-time back-and-forth conversation.
Use ai-chat for assistant conversations with streaming replies.

items.title: Comparison table
items.summary: An us versus them table with a sticky header, a highlighted column, and a stacked phone view.
uses: Showing how your product stacks up against named alternatives.
Feature matrices with three to five columns and grouped rows.
avoids: Use plan-comparison to compare your own pricing tiers.
Use a sortable data table for large datasets.

items.title: Confirm morph
items.summary: A destructive button that morphs into an inline confirmation, a spinner, and a result with undo.
uses: Deleting a selection in a table or file list, right where the button sits.
Revoking access, removing a member, or discarding a draft.
avoids: Use dialog when the consequence needs more than one line, or when typing a name to confirm is required.
Use action-button for safe async actions that need no question.

items.title: Confirm popover
items.summary: A destructive button that grows into a small confirmation card, with the consequence, optional type-to-confirm, progress on the Confirm button, and a check or error before folding back.

A row action in a table where a modal would lose the row's context.

A one word inline confirmation in a toolbar; use confirm-morph, which morphs horizontally inside the button's row.

items.title: Connected scatter

Comparing how a few segments or channels travelled through the same two metrics over the same months.

Use efficient-frontier for risk against return of a portfolio you can change.

items.title: Connector setup
items.summary: A "Connect your tools" card for an AI assistant. Each app connects inline: it redirects, authorizes and runs a first sync with a progress hairline, then lists the scopes it was granted and offers Disconnect with an inline confirm.

A first-run checklist that needs to show the OAuth handshake and first sync inline, without leaving the page.

Approving a single action the agent wants to take: use agent-approvals.

items.title: Contact section

Sales or support pages that list several channels with response times.
avoids: Use support-widget for an in-app help launcher.
Use signup-form or login blocks for account flows.

items.title: Context menu

Desktop-style right-click menus that also open from the keyboard with Shift+F10 or the ContextMenu key.

Use swipe-actions for touch-first lists like an inbox.

items.title: Context window
items.summary: An AI context window as a grid of 200 cells: the system prompt, tools, files, summary and messages fill it in order, a threshold row marks where compaction starts, and sending a message, attaching a file or compacting shows exactly how much still fits.
uses: Showing developers or power users what fills a model's context and when it will compact.
Agent and coding tools that compact long sessions and want the effect to be understandable.

Choosing a model; use model-picker.

items.title: Control center
items.summary: Workspace quick settings: tiles that morph into detail, a duration dial, and rubber-banded meters.

Focus session controls with a duration dial and allowed people.
avoids: Use switch, slider, and radio-group directly in a regular settings form.
Use time-dial to pick a time across time zones.

items.title: Cookie consent

Sites that need per-category choices with a way to reopen them later.

Use toast for a one-off message that dismisses itself.

items.summary: Copy a value with immediate confirmation.

Icon-only copy controls in dense rows, with an accessible label.

A compact deadline pill in a table row or banner.

Use photo-grid or lightbox-gallery for a large library.

When you buy, the new balance rolls in like an odometer.

A billing settings section where people also manage auto top-up and their card.

Collecting a new card number: use a card form or a hosted payment element, then pass the saved card here.

items.summary: A call to action as a centered closing section, a split beside a setup card that completes itself, or a dismissible banner.

An in-page prompt beside a product visual that shows the outcome.
avoids: The first screen of a page. Use Hero section.
Collecting an email. Use Newsletter signup.

Showcase views that cluster thousands of accounts by plan, region, or health.

Use semantic-zoom for hierarchical data like teams and projects.

Docs pages introducing an ingestion, transform, or routing concept.
avoids: Use sankey-flow to show real volumes between stages.
Use pipeline-status for the live state of a CI or data job.

items.title: Data grid
items.summary: A spreadsheet grid with range selection, inline editing, a fill handle, and animated sorting.

Data people move to and from Excel or Google Sheets with copy and paste.

Use a form when people edit one record at a time.

items.title: Date picker
items.summary: Choose a date without losing context.
uses: A date field in a form, such as a start or due date.
Dates with limits or blocked days, shown in a locale format.

Use time-picker for times, and pair it with this for a full timestamp.

items.title: Date range picker
items.summary: A range picker that grows from its trigger into two months with presets and a stretching range highlight.

Booking or leave requests where a start and end day are picked together.
avoids: Use date-picker for a single date.
Use calendar when the month should stay visible on the page.

items.title: Date reel
items.summary: A 3D wheel date and time picker (like iOS reels) with momentum scrolling, snapping, curved perspective, and full keyboard support.

Touch-first flows and mobile web, where flicking a reel beats typing a date.

items.title: Delivery tracker
items.summary: A live order tracker whose marker glides between stops while the arrival time rolls.
uses: Order status pages that follow a delivery from dispatch to door.
Tracking screens with a live arrival time and an event history.

Use progress when a single percentage is enough.

items.title: Dialog
items.summary: A focused surface for decisions that need attention.

Use bottom-sheet for mobile-first secondary tasks with snap heights.

items.title: Dictation button
items.summary: A chat composer with voice input, where the mic springs into a recording pill with a smooth live waveform, a timer, and cancel and insert buttons. Words stream into the field as you speak, muted until the recognizer settles them.

items.title: DNS resolution
items.summary: A browser asks for a domain and the query hops from the resolver to a root server, the TLD server and the authoritative nameserver, each pointing to the next, until an IP address comes back and the page connects. The resolver keeps the answer with a TTL ring that drains, and a second lookup is answered straight from that cache in one short hop.
uses: A docs or marketing section that explains how a domain name turns into an address and why the second visit is faster.
Custom domain setup, DNS hosting, resolver or CDN pages that need the chain of servers and the role of TTL to click.
avoids: Use webhook-fanout to show one event delivered to many endpoints with retries.
Use data-flow for a general pipeline between services.

items.title: Dock
items.summary: A floating tool dock with a gliding label, a springy selection, and trays that grow out of it.
uses: A floating tool or mode switcher, such as the tools of a canvas or whiteboard editor.
Toolbars where related tools share one slot and open a tray, like shape variants.
avoids: Use segmented-control for two to four inline options.
Use action-button for one-off actions that do not stay selected.

items.title: Document extraction
items.summary: Turns a document into typed data with a model and shows where every value came from: fields fill in as the page is read, and hovering a value lights its source on the PDF.

Any extraction flow where a reviewer needs to see exactly where each value came from and fix the few the model was unsure about.
avoids: Use ai-answer for a written answer with citations rather than typed fields.
Use knowledge-base to search and cite across many documents instead of reading one.

uses: Letting customers serve an app, docs site, status page or storefront from their own domain.
Verifying a sending domain for email (SPF, DKIM, DMARC) before turning on delivery.

items.title: Donut chart

A dashboard card where the total and one highlighted share matter most.

Use gauge or usage-meter for a single value against a limit.

items.title: Dot grid

items.title: Exploded view
items.summary: A scroll driven exploded view where a live phone screen built from five CSS 3D layers lies back, separates in depth with labels that follow each layer, takes each layer into focus, and then reassembles.
uses: A showpiece section that shows a product is built with care, by literally taking its screen apart.
Explaining the layers of a design system or UI kit: tokens, grid, content, controls and overlays.
avoids: Use zoom-into-ui to fly into parts of a flat product screen and explain features in place.
Use scroll-story when the story is a sequence of product states rather than the structure of one screen.

items.title: FAQ section
items.summary: FAQs as an accordion, a topic rail, or a searchable list that highlights matches.
uses: FAQ sections on pricing, product, and support pages.
Long FAQs that benefit from categories or live search.
avoids: Use accordion for generic collapsible content that is not a question list.
Use a docs page when answers need code, images, or long structure.

items.title: Feature bento
items.summary: A six cell feature bento where small, real product UI acts each feature out on hover.
uses: A landing page features section that should show the product rather than list it.
Launch pages where each capability has one clear, demonstrable behavior.
avoids: Long feature lists or comparison tables. Use Plan comparison.
A guided walkthrough with order. Use Scroll story.

items.title: Feature voting
items.summary: A public feature request board where votes roll digit by digit and the button fills with the accent. Top, New and Trending reorder the rows with one smooth move. A built-in composer suggests similar requests as you type, so people vote instead of posting duplicates.
uses: A public feature request page where customers vote and suggest ideas.
An in-app Give feedback panel that shows what is planned and shipped.
avoids: A full roadmap with columns per stage: use a kanban style board.
One off feedback on a single page or screen: use a short feedback form.

items.title: Feedback board
items.summary: A feature request board with a submit form that finds similar requests, upvotes, top and new sorting, status filters, and comments.
uses: A public or in app board where customers suggest and vote on features.
Beta programs that need a lightweight place for requests and team replies.
avoids: One to one support conversations; use support-conversation or support-widget.

items.title: File dropzone
items.summary: A generous target for dropping one or more files.
uses: Attachments and uploads with drag and drop plus a file picker.
Uploads that need per-file progress, retry, and cancel through onUpload.
avoids: Use input with type file only when a native picker with no list is enough.
Use empty-state when the drop area is the only thing on an empty page and needs a larger call to action.

items.title: File upload
items.summary: A complete file selection flow with constraints, progress, and error feedback.
uses: Uploading files with per-file progress, retry, and remove.
Attachments that must be validated by type and size before upload.
avoids: Use file-dropzone when you only need to pick files without upload state.
Use import-mapper when uploaded data needs column mapping.

items.title: Filter toolbar
items.summary: Keep collection filters close and easy to reset.
uses: Faceted filtering above tables and lists, with removable chips.
Adding filters through a two step field then value menu.
avoids: Use chip-group for a fixed set of toggles.
Use search-field for free text search.

items.title: Floating button group
items.summary: Separate soft buttons in a quiet tray, with one shared highlight that morphs from button to button as you move, and a pressed state that settles in place.
uses: A floating editor or canvas toolbar with undo, redo, share and present.
A selection toolbar that appears over text or objects.
avoids: Use toggle-group for formatting toggles or alignment where the choice stays pressed.
Use segmented-control to switch between views.

items.title: Funnel chart
items.summary: A tapered conversion funnel with drop-off at every step, a device split that morphs the band, and dots that stream through it.
uses: Conversion through a fixed sequence of steps.
Comparing how two segments convert through the same steps.
avoids: Use sankey-flow when people can branch, skip, or loop between steps.
Use bar-chart for unordered categories.

items.title: Gantt timelineNew
items.summary: A project timeline with draggable, resizable bars, dependency arrows that follow them, and animated zoom.
uses: Planning work across weeks or months where tasks depend on each other.
Roadmaps that people reschedule by dragging, with undo and conflict warnings.
avoids: Use project-board for status columns without dates.
Use week-calendar for time slots within days.

items.title: Gauge
items.summary: Show a value against a known range.
uses: One value against a known range, such as disk quota or health score.
Values with labelled bands, like Healthy, Filling up, and Critical.
avoids: Use progress for task completion.
Use usage-meter for plan limits and activity-rings for several goals at once.

items.title: Generation stats
items.summary: A live stats strip for a streaming LLM response where time to first token, speed with a sparkline, output tokens and cost count up in tabular numerals beside the model's real mark, then settle and open into a latency and token cost breakdown.
uses: Under assistant messages in a chat product that shows people what a response cost or how fast it was.
Playgrounds, eval runners and internal dev panels comparing models on latency, throughput and cost.
avoids: Use context-window to show how much of a model's context a conversation has used.
Use a chart or table for spend across many requests or days; this strip describes one response.

items.title: Ghost mascot
items.summary: A floating ghost mascot whose soft sheet ripples at the hem while it hovers. It blinks when idle, turns toward you to listen, fades a little translucent while thinking, draws a tiny pen line while writing, smiles with a sparkle when done and wobbles once on an error.
uses: Give an assistant a light, friendly face that shows what it is doing: in a reply header, in a composer, over an image canvas while it generates, or in an empty state.
Products that want generation to feel alive without a spinner, with states that still read at 24px.
avoids: Use agent-status when people need the steps, tools and elapsed time of a run, not just a mood.
Use text-shimmer alone for a plain "Thinking" line in dense interfaces where a character would distract.

items.title: Ghost text
items.summary: An inline AI autocomplete where muted ghost text continues your sentence exactly at the caret and Tab turns it solid in place. Cmd+Right takes it one word at a time, Escape fades it away, and a calm chip shows the model behind it.
uses: Long-form fields people write in product: pull request descriptions, emails, support replies, issue bodies, release notes, CRM notes.
Short single-line fields where a likely completion saves typing, such as an email subject or a commit message.
avoids: Use ai-composer for a chat-style prompt box that sends a message to an assistant.
Use code-suggestion for code diffs with accept and reject per hunk.

items.title: Glass card
items.summary: A glass info panel over a photo whose rim catches a pointer-following highlight while the card tilts; tap to morph it into a detail sheet.
uses: Profile, host, or creator cards on a landing page or in a discovery grid.
A featured product or stay where the photo sells and the details can wait for a tap.
avoids: Dense grids of many cards; tilt and glass on every tile gets busy. Use card.
Cards that should open a full page; use card-to-article.

items.title: Glass menu
items.summary: A glass action menu whose trigger morphs into the panel, with a highlight pill that glides between rows, one in-place submenu, and full keyboard support.
uses: Actions for a photo, file, or card shown over an image or a colorful canvas.
A title menu in an editor or viewer, where the title itself opens the actions.
avoids: Plain settings pages with no imagery behind the menu. Use dropdown-menu on a neutral surface.
Navigation between pages. Use morph-nav or tabs.

items.title: Glass segmented
items.summary: A glass segmented control whose liquid indicator stretches between segments and can be dragged and flung.
uses: Switching the view of a photo, map, or media surface.
A compact filter over imagery, such as day, week, month on a hero chart.
avoids: Plain forms on neutral surfaces. Use segmented-control.
More than five options or long labels. Use tabs or a select.

items.title: Glass tab bar
items.summary: A floating Liquid Glass tab bar that refracts what scrolls beneath it, with a glass lens that glides, magnifies and can be dragged between tabs, and an optional search bubble; it compacts on scroll down.
uses: Mobile web apps and PWAs with three to five top level sections and one global action such as search.
Content feeds where the bar should step aside while reading and come back on scroll up.
avoids: Desktop layouts with many sections; use a sidebar or morph-nav.
Switching views inside a card; use segmented-control or tabs.

items.title: Goal tracker
items.summary: A team goals card where objectives open into key results with owners, confidence and progress bars. A weekly check-in updates a value, confidence and note in place, fills the bar and recalculates the objective, and a quarter selector steps from last quarter's final scores to next quarter's planning.
uses: Showing a team's quarterly objectives and key results with owners and confidence.
Collecting a lightweight weekly check-in (value, confidence, note) without leaving the page.
avoids: A single KPI with a trend line; use a metric or stat card.
Task or project tracking with assignees and due dates; use a task list or kanban block.

items.title: Gravity well
items.summary: A grid of tiles that bends toward the cursor like spacetime, with a click that sends a shockwave through it.
uses: A team, customer, or moodboard wall where playfulness is the point.
Landing page sections that show breadth: many logos, avatars, or photos at once.
avoids: Grids people must scan or click precisely, like file pickers; use a plain grid.
Large collections; use infinite-moodboard or photo-grid.

items.title: Help center
items.summary: A help center with instant search, topic cards, and popular articles that open into a readable article with an outline and feedback.
uses: A public help center or knowledge base
In-app help with searchable articles
avoids: Developer API reference with a nav tree, use docs-sidebar
A short FAQ on a marketing page, use faq-section

items.title: Hero section
items.summary: Three full screen SaaS heroes: a live dashboard rising from the bottom edge over a drifting mesh, a workflow graph that routes sample events node by node, and editorial type over a mesh gradient.
uses: The first section of a SaaS landing page, when the product screen is the pitch (Screenshot).
Developer tools, automation, and infrastructure products, where showing the product working is the pitch (Workflow).
avoids: Use page-header for titles inside app screens.
Use hero-signup when the goal is collecting an email in the first section.

items.title: Hero signup
items.summary: A full screen waitlist hero on a soft, drifting mesh gradient: the email field validates as you type and its button grows into the confirmation with your place in line.
uses: Waitlists, early access, and launch pages where the email is the only ask.
Pages that want a calm but alive first impression without product screenshots.
avoids: Signup that needs a password, SSO choice, or consent up front; use Sign up form.
A newsletter box further down the page; use Newsletter signup.

items.title: Hold to confirm
items.summary: Confirm a destructive action by holding, not tapping.
uses: Destructive actions like delete or revoke where the consequence is already visible on screen.
Replacing a confirm dialog with a deliberate press in compact settings rows.
avoids: Use dialog when people need to read what will happen before confirming.
Use button or action-button for safe, easily undone actions.

items.title: Holo card
items.summary: A member card that tilts toward you with a holographic foil and flips to its back.
uses: A membership or subscription card on an account or welcome page.
A shareable profile, badge, or achievement that people will screenshot.
avoids: Use card for ordinary content; the effect is too loud for lists.
Use depth-cards when several items need a subtle parallax.

items.title: Horizon chart
items.summary: A horizon chart that stacks fourteen daily series as compact folded rows, with a synced crosshair, a sort by name, peak or latest, a band count setting that folds every row on one spring, and a legend that explains how to read the bands.
uses: Operations or growth dashboards comparing many markets, services or products against their own baseline over weeks or months.
Monitoring views where the reader scans for which rows broke from normal and when, then reads exact values on one day.
avoids: Use small-multiples when there are only a few series and the reader needs axes and exact levels in each panel.
Use ridgeline to compare distributions rather than values over time.

items.title: Hover card
items.summary: Preview a person or link on hover or focus without leaving the page.
uses: Previews of people behind mentions, avatars, or author names.
Link or reference previews where the click must stay free for navigation.
avoids: Use tooltip for a plain text label.
Use popover when the content has buttons or inputs.

items.title: Icon morph
items.summary: Icons that morph between states: menu to close, play to pause, copy to check, and more.
uses: Icon buttons that toggle between two states, such as a hamburger menu or a play control.
Copy and add actions that should confirm with a check in place.
avoids: Use copy-button for a complete copy-to-clipboard control with its own feedback.
Use theme-switch for a labelled light and dark toggle wired to the page theme.

items.title: Image compare
items.summary: Drag a divider across two images to see what changed.
uses: Before and after visuals such as photo edits, redesigns, or cleanup results.
Top and bottom comparisons, via orientation vertical.
avoids: Use carousel to browse many images.
Use resizable-panels to split live content rather than images.

items.title: Image generation
items.summary: An image studio where each image forms on a dot matrix: a soft halftone wave breathes across the grid, the dots take the colours of the coming photo and grow into a coloured halftone, then blur away into the sharp photo. One large canvas with a mono size label, a filmstrip of four variations, a prompt bar with model and ratio, and upscale with a sweeping dot band, vary or download, with real provider marks and a built-in simulation.
uses: A text to image feature inside a product: marketing asset tools, listing photo helpers, slide or doc illustration.
Any flow where people compare a few candidates and continue with one (upscale, vary, download).
avoids: A full canvas editor with layers, masks and inpainting; build on a canvas library instead.
Drawing a sketch to turn into an image; use sketch-to-image.

items.title: Image reveal
items.summary: An image generation canvas where a soft, blurred preview made from the image's own colors sharpens top to bottom behind a soft-edged band. It works the way ChatGPT, Midjourney and Gemini show images forming, with fine film grain, a translucent progress pill and calm queued and error states.
uses: Showing an image model's progress on a canvas or in a chat reply.
A batch of image variations sampling side by side.
avoids: Plain image loading from a CDN; use a blur-up placeholder or a skeleton.
Text generation or tool calls; use text-shimmer or tool-call.

items.title: Image trail
items.summary: Moving the pointer leaves a curated trail of photos that pop in, lean, and fade away.
uses: A portfolio or agency hero that should feel alive on first move.
Travel, food, or product stories told through a sequence of photos.
avoids: Use photo-grid or lightbox-gallery when people need to look at each photo.
Use hover-image-list to preview one image per row in a list.

items.title: In-view title
items.summary: Bring a section title in as it scrolls into view.
uses: Section headings that should animate once they scroll into view.
Feature pages where each section title needs a consistent entrance style.
avoids: Use text-reveal for hero copy that animates on load.
Use scroll-highlight for a paragraph that follows scroll progress.

items.title: Inbox triage
items.summary: Process a focused inbox with archive, snooze, and restore actions.
uses: A queue of messages or requests that need archive, snooze, or restore decisions.
Inboxes where rows expand in place to show details and actions.
avoids: Use inbox-sidebar for mail navigation with folders and counts.
Use notification-center for system notifications.

items.title: Ink fluid
items.summary: A real time fluid simulation behind your hero: the cursor stirs soft ink that swirls, settles and fades; calm when left alone.
uses: A landing hero or sign in screen that should feel alive without a video.
Empty states and waiting screens where a gentle, interactive background rewards curiosity.
avoids: Dense product surfaces such as tables and forms. Movement behind data distracts.
More than one per page; each instance runs its own simulation.

items.title: Inline edit
items.summary: Rename in place: the text becomes a field without moving.
uses: Titles and descriptions read far more often than edited, like a project name.
Single fields that save on their own with optimistic updates and rollback.
avoids: Use input or textarea in a form when several fields save together.
Use input when the field should always look editable.

items.title: Input
items.summary: A single line field with clear labels and useful states.
uses: Any single-line text value in a form, such as name, email, or URL.
Fields whose helper or error copy changes as the person types, where the message should reword in place.
avoids: Use textarea for multi-line text.
Use password-field, search-field, or number-field when the value has that shape.

items.title: Install snippet
items.summary: A "get started in 30 seconds" card where framework tabs, three numbered steps and highlighted snippets take a developer from install to first event. Generate key wipes a fresh API key into the placeholder in place.
uses: A quickstart that has to work for several frameworks without three pages of docs.
Onboarding where creating an API key is part of getting started.
avoids: A single code sample with no steps: use code-block.
Trying requests against a live API: use api-playground.

items.title: Integrations
items.summary: An integrations directory where Connect morphs to Connected and the filters recount as you go.
uses: Settings or marketplace pages for third party connections.
Directories with search, category filters, and Connect buttons.
avoids: Use webhooks for outgoing event endpoints.
Use api-keys for developer credentials.

items.title: Invite people
items.summary: Invite teammates with roles, bulk paste validation, a seat meter, and avatars that fly into a pending list.
uses: Inviting several people at once by name or email, with a role for each.
Plans with a seat limit where people should see the effect of an invite before sending.
avoids: Use team-members to manage people who already joined.
Use roles-permissions to edit what each role can do.

items.title: Invoice studio
items.summary: An editable invoice with live totals and a clear save flow.
uses: Creating or editing an invoice or quote with line items.
Forms that need a live subtotal and total as quantities and rates change.
avoids: Use billing-overview to show past invoices and plan status.
Use checkout-flow when the customer is paying.

items.title: Journey flow
items.summary: A Sankey of user journeys whose flows morph by channel and trace a cohort on hover.
uses: Showing where users go between funnel stages, such as visit to signup to activation.
Comparing flows across acquisition channels with a segment switch.
avoids: Use cohort-retention to show how groups retain over time.
Use bar-chart for a simple linear funnel without branching paths.

items.title: JSON viewer
items.summary: A collapsible JSON tree with search, paging for long arrays, and copy value or path.
uses: Inspecting a JSON payload in a developer dashboard, such as webhooks or API logs.
Large nested objects where search and copy path save time.
avoids: Use code-block to show JSON as formatted source for copying whole.
Use tree-view for folders, navigation, or other non-JSON hierarchies.

items.title: Kanban board
items.summary: A kanban board where cards lift, tilt and spring into the slot that opens for them, with swimlanes and live WIP limits.
uses: A team board where cards move between statuses.
Pipelines where ordering within a stage matters.
avoids: Scheduling on dates; use gantt-timeline or week-calendar.
Read only status summaries; use a table.

items.title: Keycap keyboard
items.summary: Mechanical keycaps that sink and light up as you type, with the text above the board.
uses: Landing pages for keyboard-first products and developer tools.
Onboarding that teaches shortcuts by lighting the keys they use.
avoids: Form input; use a real text field.
On-screen keyboards for accessibility needs; use the platform's.

items.title: Knowledge base
items.summary: A retrieval knowledge base in one card: add sources and watch them parse, chunk, embed and index, then test a question and see which chunks come back and why.
uses: Admin screens for a RAG or support assistant where people add documents, watch them index, and check what a question retrieves.
Explaining or tuning chunking, hybrid search and reranking with a working test bench instead of a diagram.
avoids: Use vector-search to illustrate how embeddings and nearest neighbours work; this block is the working product surface.
Use document-extract to pull structured fields out of a single document.

items.title: KPI drilldown
items.summary: KPI cards that expand into a full detail chart with period comparison and a breakdown table, then fold back.
uses: An analytics or finance overview where each number deserves a closer look.
Executive dashboards that compare the current period with the previous one.
avoids: Use metric-explorer to compare many metrics on one chart.
Use metrics-dashboard for a static summary without drill down.

items.title: Layout morph
items.summary: A 24 card gallery that flies between grid, masonry, list, fan, carousel and a 3D helix.
uses: Catalogue, portfolio, or team pages where people browse the same set in different layouts.
Showcase galleries that fly between grid, masonry, list, fan, carousel, and a 3D helix.
avoids: Use photo-grid for a simple gallery.
Use carousel or cover-flow for one horizontal browsing style.

items.title: Lead scoring
items.summary: A lead scoring card where inbound B2B leads are ranked by an AI fit score, each with a score ring and a one-line reason. Open a lead to see its signals and score breakdown, then push it to HubSpot or Salesforce.
uses: A sales inbox or SDR queue that ranks new inbound leads by fit.
Showing why a model scored a lead, with signals and a weighted breakdown.
avoids: Large tables of hundreds of leads with filters and bulk edits; use a data table.
Enriching columns of company data; use enrich-column.

items.title: Lightbox gallery
items.summary: A masonry grid where photos zoom from their slot into a viewer you can swipe, pinch, and drag away.
uses: Photo collections people browse and inspect up close, such as trips, portfolios, or listings.
Mixed portrait and landscape sets that should keep their aspect ratios in a masonry grid.
avoids: Use photo-grid for a square grid with pinch zoom between densities.
Use carousel for a single inline row without a viewer.

items.title: Line chart
items.summary: A multi-series line chart with a gliding crosshair, legend toggles, and paths that morph between ranges.
uses: Traffic, revenue, or latency over days or weeks in a dashboard card.
Comparing this period against a previous period or target with a dashed series.
avoids: Use sparkline for a tiny inline trend with no axes or tooltip.
Use bar-chart for discrete categories or counts per bucket.

items.title: Line replay
items.summary: A time replay line chart that draws a day of traffic with a moving playhead, a value label on the tip, a scrubber, speed control and key moments annotated as the playhead passes them.
uses: Post-launch or campaign reviews where the team wants to watch traffic respond to each announcement.
Incident retrospectives that step through a metric with the alert, the deploy and the recovery marked.
avoids: Use annotated-trend when people need to add and edit their own notes on a static trend.
Use connected-scatter to replay how two measures moved together over time.

items.title: Link unfurl
items.summary: A composer where pasting a URL shows a loading shimmer on the link, then unfurls it into a rich preview card with title, image and favicon in one morph, which can be collapsed back to the inline link or removed.
uses: A message or comment composer where pasted links should show what they point to before sending.
Product marketing that shows how a chat or notes app handles links.
avoids: Use hover-card to preview a link someone reads, not writes.
Use mention-input when the tokens are people or records rather than web links, and rich-text-editor for long formatted documents.

items.title: Liquid tab bar
items.summary: Tabs with a lens selection that slides between them, swaps labels cleanly, and fills in icons as it passes.
uses: Switching between a handful of peer sections with icons, such as an app's main areas.
Bottom or top bars on mobile-style layouts where the selection should feel physical.
avoids: Use tabs for text-only panels inside a page.
Use segmented-control for compact filters or view toggles.

items.title: Live visitors
items.summary: A realtime visitors card where the live count rolls digit by digit, new arrivals ping in on a dotted world map, the top pages reorder with bars, and signups and upgrades tick in with country flags.
uses: Realtime visitors on a marketing site or app, next to signups and upgrades as they happen.
Launch days and campaigns where a team watches traffic and conversions live.
avoids: Historical trends over days or weeks; use a chart with axes.
Precise geography or per-country breakdowns; use a table or a proper map.

items.title: LLM cost calculator
items.summary: A pricing calculator for LLM workloads. Set tokens per request, requests per day and prompt caching, and eight current models re-rank by monthly cost. Bars glide and prices roll as you drag.
uses: A pricing or settings page needs an honest monthly estimate for an LLM workload across several models.
People pick a model for a feature and should see how cost moves with prompt size, output length, traffic and caching.
avoids: Use model-picker to choose a model in a chat or composer without a cost comparison.
Use context-window to show the live token usage of one conversation against a model's context window.

items.title: Login and sign up5, free and Pro variants
items.summary: Sign in and sign up pages, from a compact code card to full screen split and immersive layouts.

items.title: Centered login
items.summary: A passkey-first login card on a quiet ring backdrop that morphs through email and code.

items.title: Logo marquee
items.summary: A quiet, continuously moving row of brand marks with a pause control.
uses: A customer or integration logo strip on a landing page.
Social proof sections with a heading and a short supporting line.
avoids: Use integrations when each logo needs a description or a connect action.
