Use testimonial-stage when quotes matter more than logos.

items.title: Magic link
items.summary: A passwordless sign in card where an email with inline validation and typo fixes sends a magic link, and the card crossfades in place to a check your inbox step with a sealing envelope, Gmail and Outlook shortcuts and a resend countdown. Google and GitHub sign in sit above, with their real marks.
uses: Passwordless sign in or sign up by email link, with optional Google and GitHub sign in.
B2B products that want a work email gate with a clear what happens next screen.
avoids: Password plus email sign in or MFA codes; use sign-in or a login block instead.
One time codes typed into the app; use an OTP input flow.

items.title: Market terminal
items.summary: A trading terminal with a canvas candlestick chart, volume, moving averages, crosshair OHLC readout, wheel, drag and pinch zoom, a live watchlist with sparklines and flashing prices, and a market and limit order ticket.
uses: A trading or investing product that needs a full chart, a watchlist and an order ticket on one screen.
A paper trading or education app where people practice placing market and limit orders against moving prices.
avoids: Use order-book-depth to show bids and asks at each price level.
Use metric-explorer or a line chart for product or business metrics without open, high, low and close.

items.title: MCP servers
items.summary: Manage the MCP servers that give an agent its tools: see what the enabled tools cost in context, connect or pause a server, and switch single tools on or off.
uses: Settings for an agent or AI assistant that connects to MCP servers: which servers it has, which tools are on and what they cost in context.
Onboarding a new integration with a directory, sign in and tool discovery in one place.
avoids: Use agent-approvals to approve or deny individual tool calls while the agent runs.
Use context-window to show everything in the context window, not only tool definitions.

items.title: Media player
items.summary: An audio player with a living playlist and complete playback controls.
uses: A small audio collection such as a podcast, sample pack, or playlist.
Pages that need a full player with seek, skip, volume, and a track list.
avoids: Use now-playing for a compact now playing widget.
Use transcript-studio when the audio needs a synced transcript.

items.title: Meeting summary
items.summary: An AI meeting notes card: the header shows the Google Meet or Zoom mark, the attendees and the duration. Summary, Decisions and Action items stream in after a short summarizing pass. Hover any line to see the transcript quote it came from, then check off action items or send them to Linear or Notion.
uses: Showing AI notes after a call in a CRM, a recruiting tool, a meeting recorder or a team workspace.
Turning a transcript into decisions and owned tasks that people can push to their tracker.
avoids: Live captions or a running transcript during the call; use text-stream or a transcript view.
A general task list with no meeting behind it; use checkbox rows in your own list.

items.title: Mega menu morph
items.summary: A site header whose menus share one floating panel. Moving between sections morphs its size, slides the next menu in from that side and glides the caret under the new trigger, with hover intent, a safe triangle and an accordion sheet on narrow screens.
uses: A marketing site header with product, solution, developer and company sections that each need a rich menu.
A documentation or platform site whose top sections deserve descriptions, a featured story or a status line.
avoids: Use morph-nav for a compact floating pill navigation with search built in.
Use dropdown-menu for a single list of actions or links behind one button.

items.title: Mention input
items.summary: A textarea with @people and #channel mentions that act as single tokens, with suggestions at the caret.
uses: Comment and reply boxes where people are tagged with @ and should be notified by id.
Chat or task composers that link #channels or projects inline.
avoids: Use textarea for plain notes with no references.
Use tag-input when the tokens are a separate list rather than part of a sentence.

items.title: Metric card
items.summary: A compact summary for a number that needs context.
uses: A single plain number with odometer style rolling digits, such as uptime or orders.
Numbers that update live and should roll in the direction they moved.
avoids: Use stat-card for preformatted strings, trend arrows, tones, and icons.
Use sparkline when the trend over time matters more than the latest value.

items.title: Metric explorer
items.summary: KPI cards that open into a scrubbable chart and morph between metrics and ranges.
uses: The top of a SaaS analytics or finance page with KPI cards that open into a chart.
Dashboards where people move between a few metrics and date ranges.
avoids: Use stat-card or metric-card for static KPI tiles.
Use revenue-explorer for a revenue breakdown with a range brush.

items.title: Metric ticker
items.summary: A strip of live KPIs that roll to new values digit by digit and flash their change; rest on one to pause the strip and open its recent trend as a sparkline.
uses: A compact live readout of several KPIs above a dashboard, a status page or a trading view.
Wall screens and operations views where values change on their own and people glance at them.
avoids: Use metric-card or stat-card for one or two headline numbers with room for context.
Use line-chart or sparkline when the trend over time is the main content, not a detail.

items.title: Metrics dashboard
items.summary: A dense analytics view with KPI tabs, one inspectable chart, and top pages and sources.
uses: A small, explorable KPI overview with a range toggle and one chart.
Product or marketing dashboards with four headline metrics, a 7, 30, or 90 day range, and top pages and sources.
avoids: Use metric-explorer or revenue-explorer for larger or drill-down data.
Use stat-card for a single number.

items.title: Mixture of experts
items.summary: An illustration of mixture of experts routing: each token is scored by a router, travels to its top experts, and their outputs merge into the token's result.
uses: Explaining why a mixture of experts model is cheap per token: only the chosen experts run, which the active parameter readout makes concrete.
Showing how a gate scores experts, picks the top k and blends their outputs, with real or sample scores.
avoids: Use model-router to pick which model handles a request in a product; this card explains routing inside one model.
Use attention-map to show which tokens a token attends to, rather than which experts process it.

items.title: Model arena
items.summary: A blind side by side model comparison in one card: send one prompt to two models, watch both answers stream at the same pace, vote for the better one, then reveal which model wrote each.
uses: Blind human preference tests between two models on the same prompt, such as an internal bake-off before switching providers.
Prompt or model evaluation tools where people should judge answers without knowing which model wrote them.
avoids: Use model-picker to let someone choose one model for their own chat; this block compares answers, it does not set a default.
Use eval-suite to score many prompts automatically against expected outputs rather than collecting one human vote at a time.

items.title: Model card
items.summary: A model details card where switching models rolls every price, limit and score in place, a token slider estimates monthly cost live, and benchmark bars show each model's rank on hover. Compare crossfades to a side-by-side table against any rival with the better values marked, and the card never changes size.
uses: The detail pane of a model picker, showing what the highlighted model can do and what it costs before someone selects it.
Model pages in docs or a marketplace, with limits, prices and a quick benchmark read against close rivals.
avoids: Use model-picker to choose between many models; pair it with this card for the details.
Use context-window to show how full a live conversation's context is.

items.title: Model picker
items.summary: A model picker in one quiet pill: open it to choose from featured models with a one line note each, set the reasoning effort, or browse every other model by provider, and the pill swaps to your choice in place.
uses: Choosing the model and effort for a chat, an agent or a playground.
A default model setting with a short review of what the chosen model costs and how much context it takes.
avoids: Comparing two models' answers side by side; use model-arena.
A full prompt box with attachments and tools; use ai-composer, which has its own model chip.

items.title: Model training
items.summary: Training data batches feed a small neural net diagram whose connections strengthen, a loss curve descends beside it, and an evaluation check turns green at the end.
uses: An AI or ML product section that explains training, fine-tuning or evaluation in one glance.
Docs pages introducing batches, epochs, loss curves or held-out evaluation.
avoids: Use line-chart or metric-card for real, live training metrics.
Use data-flow to explain how records move through a pipeline, and pipeline-status for real job status.

items.title: Money input
items.summary: A currency field with live grouping, stable width, rolling digits, and minor-unit output.
uses: Payment, tip, transfer, or budget amounts entered by hand.
Invoice and expense forms where the currency may change.
avoids: Use number-field for quantities and non currency numbers.
Use slider or price-ladder when people pick from a range rather than type.

items.title: Morph loader
items.summary: Tiny loaders that morph between shapes and fold into a check or a cross when done.
uses: Inline progress inside a button, row, or field where the result should appear in the same spot.
Short operations that end in a clear success or failure, such as save, publish, or upload.
avoids: Use progress when the percentage is known.
Use skeleton when content is loading into a layout.

items.title: Morph nav
items.summary: A navigation bar that morphs into rich menus, search, and a compact state as one surface.
uses: The top navigation of a marketing or product site with a few sections that each hold several destinations.
Headers where search should grow out of the bar instead of opening a separate modal.
avoids: Use liquid-tab-bar for an app-style switcher between a handful of peer sections.
Use tabs for switching views inside a page.

items.title: Morph select
items.summary: A select whose trigger grows into the list, with a gliding highlight and type-ahead.
uses: Form fields and property panels where one value is picked from a known list.
Grouped lists like time zones, assignees, or projects, with optional icons and meta.
avoids: Use combobox when users type free text or the list is very long and remote.
Use multi-select when more than one value can be chosen.

items.title: MRR waterfall
items.summary: An MRR bridge whose floating bars morph by period and open the accounts behind each move.
uses: Revenue or board reporting that explains how MRR moved from start to end of a period.
Finance views where each movement should list the accounts behind it.
avoids: Use revenue-explorer for MRR over many months.
Use bar-chart for plain comparisons that do not build from a start value.

items.title: Multi-region failover
items.summary: Animated multi-region failover on a 2.5D stage: users stream requests through a global load balancer to two regions; the primary degrades, fails three health checks, traffic shifts smoothly to the healthy region, then it recovers, passes three checks and traffic ramps back to an even split.
uses: A reliability, infrastructure or pricing page that needs to show why running in two regions keeps a service up during an outage.
Docs for health checks, failover policies, traffic weights or slow start, where viewers should step through detection, failover, recovery and rebalance.
avoids: Use database-replication to show a primary database failing over to a replica.
Use circuit-breaker for one service failing fast against a failing dependency.

items.title: Multi-select
items.summary: Select several values while keeping the field readable.
uses: Picking several values from a fixed list in a compact field, such as labels or assignees.
Filters where the chosen values should show in the field with a +N overflow.
avoids: Use chip-group when every option should stay visible.
Use tag-input for free-form values.

items.title: Multi-step form
items.summary: A guided form that presents one decision at a time and preserves progress.
uses: Onboarding or intake flows split into a few short steps.
Wizards that need Back and Continue, progress, and a success state out of the box.
avoids: Use stepper when you only need the progress indicator.
Use checkout-flow for full page flows.

items.title: Newsletter signup
items.summary: An email signup framed by a stack of past issues; subscribing drops the next issue, addressed to you, onto the front.
uses: Collecting emails for a newsletter, digest, or changelog that has real issues to show.
The end of a blog post or docs page.
avoids: Account creation with a password. Use Signup form.
Longer forms with several fields. Use Contact section.

items.title: Notification center
items.summary: A home for updates with read state, grouped information, and animated disclosure.
uses: A bell in the app header with an unread badge and an inbox of recent updates.
Notifications people can mark read, expand, and dismiss in bulk.
avoids: Use toast-stack for transient messages that should disappear.
Use inbox-triage for a full-page inbox.

items.title: Now playing
items.summary: Grow a mini player into the full player in one continuous morph.
uses: Media that keeps playing while people browse, such as music, podcasts, or audio lessons.
A mini player bar that expands into a full player with artwork and a scrubber.
avoids: Use bottom-sheet or dialog for a one-off overlay that is not a player.
Use voice-recorder for recording and playing back short voice notes.

items.title: Number field
items.summary: Enter a bounded number with clear increment controls.
uses: Bounded quantities like seats, items, or prices where the exact number matters.
Values people nudge with steppers, arrow keys, or by dragging the label with scrub.
avoids: Use slider when the approximate position matters more than the exact number.
Use input for numeric strings like phone numbers or codes.

items.title: Onboarding checklist
items.summary: Guide a new workspace through setup, one step at a time.
uses: A one-time getting-started card with three to eight loosely ordered steps.
Setup steps that run async actions, like Connect GitHub, and check off when they resolve.
avoids: Use stepper when the order is strict and steps map to screens.
Use multi-step-form when every step collects form input.

items.title: Onboarding illustration
items.summary: A compact onboarding card whose line illustration morphs from folder to files, team, and badge.
uses: A short first-run dialog in a document or workspace product.
Onboarding with three or four steps that each need a simple picture.
avoids: Use onboarding-checklist for tasks people complete over time.
Use feature-illustration for a feature section on a marketing page.

items.title: Onboarding survey
items.summary: A post-signup onboarding survey where each question gets its own step of large option cards, picked with keys 1 to 4 and Enter. A short personalization checklist then ticks off and lands on an editable "You're all set" summary.
uses: Post-signup personalization: role, team size and first action before the first screen.
Short in-product surveys where every answer changes what someone sees next.
avoids: Long forms with free text or many fields; use a regular form or import-wizard.
Guided tours over the real interface; use onboarding-tour.

items.title: Orbit logos
items.summary: An integrations showcase with brand logos orbiting your product mark on tilted rings. Hover or focus one to rest the orbit, draw a connection, and see what it does.
uses: An integrations or ecosystem hero on a marketing site.
An integrations settings screen where people browse, read about, and connect tools.
avoids: Use a logo marquee for a long list of customer logos.
Use a searchable grid or table for catalogs larger than about twenty integrations.

items.title: Orbit menu
items.summary: Hold a button and its actions orbit out, ready to pick with a drag.
uses: Three to six quick actions on one object, such as a note or photo.
Touch-first surfaces where press, drag, and release should fire an action in one gesture.
avoids: Use dropdown-menu or context-menu for longer or text-heavy lists.
Use dock for tools that stay selected.

items.title: OTP input
items.summary: A six digit verification flow with paste support and keyboard navigation.
uses: Verification codes from email or SMS.
Two-factor authentication code entry.
avoids: Use password-field for secrets people type from memory.
Use input for any other text.

items.title: Page curl
items.summary: A small magazine you read by dragging page corners, with a real fold, lit curl, and flick to turn.
uses: Editorial and brand showcases where paper is part of the story.
Menus, catalogs, and yearbooks with a handful of spreads.
avoids: Use carousel or a scrolling page for long content or content people search.
Use a document viewer for dense text that needs zoom and selection.

items.title: Page header
items.summary: A project page header that folds into a compact bar as you scroll, with tabs whose counts roll.
uses: The top of a project, repository, or record page with breadcrumbs, status, people, and tabs.
Detail pages with long content where the header should fold into a compact bar as people scroll.
avoids: Use tabs and breadcrumb on their own when the page only needs navigation, not status and people.
Use workspace-sidebar for app-level navigation between sections.

items.title: Pagination
items.summary: Move through a long collection with clear bounds.
uses: Paged server results and long tables.
Lists where the page should live in the URL or state and fetch on change.
avoids: Use carousel for browsing slides.
Use timeline with maxHeight for a scrolling feed instead of pages.

items.title: Password field
items.summary: Capture sensitive text with a visible reveal control.
uses: Sign in forms and password confirmation fields.
Any secret the person may want to check by revealing it.
avoids: Use password-strength when creating or changing a password.
Use input for non-secret values.

items.title: Password strength
items.summary: Show how strong a new password is while it is typed.
uses: Sign up and change password forms.
Password rules that should check off live as the person types.
avoids: Use password-field for sign in.
Use progress for measurable progress unrelated to passwords.

items.title: Payment flow
items.summary: A card tap goes to a processor, then the network, then the bank and back with authorization, then settlement; each hop lights up with a status label and the amount travels as a chip.
uses: A payments or checkout landing section that explains authorization and settlement.
Docs pages introducing processors, card networks, issuers, fees, and payout timing.
avoids: Use checkout-flow or checkout-live for a real checkout form.
Use webhook-fanout to explain what happens after a payment event is emitted.

items.title: Phone input
items.summary: A phone field with a country picker, formatting as you type, and E.164 output.
uses: Sign up, checkout, and contact forms that need a phone number in E.164.
International audiences where the country and calling code must be clear.
avoids: Use input with type="tel" when you only store free text and never dial or text the number.
Use otp-input for the verification code itself.

items.title: Photo grid
items.summary: Pinch through zoom levels and open any photo straight from its cell.
uses: A browsable photo library or album where people zoom between column counts.
Galleries that need favorites and a full-screen viewer with a filmstrip.
avoids: Use lightbox-gallery for a masonry layout that keeps each photo's aspect ratio.
Use carousel for a short inline slideshow.

items.title: PII redaction
items.summary: A guardrail card where personal data is redacted before the prompt reaches the model. Scan marks each name, email, phone number and card with its type and swaps it for a placeholder like [EMAIL_1]. The safe prompt travels to Claude, and the reply comes back with the original values put back for the person.
uses: Explaining or proving a privacy guardrail in an AI product: support assistants, health or finance copilots, enterprise chat.
A settings or onboarding screen where admins see what the PII filter does before they turn it on.
avoids: Use ai-chat or ai-composer for the conversation itself; redact behind the scenes and show this card only where the guardrail needs explaining.
Do not rely on the built-in detector for compliance; pass a real DLP service through detect.

items.title: Pixel mascot
items.summary: A pixel-art robot that shows what an AI assistant is doing. It idles, thinks, types, celebrates and errors in frame-stepped sprite animations, and stays crisp at every integer size from 24px to 192px.
uses: A friendly generating indicator next to an assistant reply or in a chat composer.
An empty state or onboarding panel where a small character makes an AI feature feel approachable.
avoids: Detailed agent progress with steps and timings; use agent-status or agent-timeline.
Dense tables or toolbars where a 24px character is noise; use status-dot or a spinner.

items.title: Plan comparison
items.summary: Compare meaningful differences between plans and billing periods.
uses: Comparing two tiers side by side with a feature matrix.
Pricing pages that switch between monthly and yearly prices.
avoids: Use usage-pricing when price depends on seats or volume.
Use segmented-control alone for a simple billing toggle.

items.title: Popover
items.summary: A small anchored surface for contextual information.
uses: Click-opened panels with interactive content, like share settings or a small filter form.
Non-modal helpers that should stay open while people interact with the rest of the page.
avoids: Use tooltip for short hover labels.
Use hover-card for read-only previews that open on hover.

items.title: Presence stack
items.summary: Avatars of the people here now: joins pop in as the stack reflows, a counter rolls past the limit, dots show typing and idle, and hover fans it out with a gliding name label.
uses: A document, board or design file header that shows who is here right now.
A call or meeting roster where people come and go and some are talking or idle.
avoids: Use avatar-group for a static list of owners, assignees or members that does not change while you look at it.
Use live-cursors when you also need cursors and selections on a canvas; it includes its own small stack.

items.title: Pricing calculator
items.summary: A seat slider and billing toggle drive plan cards with rolling prices and a moving recommended badge.
uses: Per-seat pricing where showing the exact total for a team size helps people choose.
Pricing pages with a monthly and yearly toggle and a visible yearly saving.
avoids: Use usage-pricing when price depends on metered usage rather than seats.
Use plan-comparison for a feature by feature table across plans.

items.title: Prize wheel
items.summary: A referral or promo prize wheel you flick to spin, with real angular momentum, a flexible pointer that ticks against each peg, weighted segments set by the host, a slow suspenseful settle, and the won segment lifting into a reward card with a copyable code.
uses: A referral or launch page that rewards a signup with a discount code.
An in-product moment that grants one of several perks, such as a milestone reward.
avoids: Use a plain coupon card or copy button when everyone gets the same reward.
Avoid it in serious flows such as billing or checkout, where chance feels out of place.

items.title: Product detail
items.summary: A product page with a swipeable gallery, finish and size variants, add to bag that confirms in place, shipping, a reviews summary, and details.
uses: Product pages with a few variants, a gallery, and reviews.
Stores that want stock aware variants with a restock alert instead of a dead button.
avoids: Products built from many options with live pricing; use product-configurator.
Browsing many products; use product-listing.

items.title: Product gallery
items.summary: A product gallery with a hover magnifier, gliding thumbnails, and color and size variants that crossfade photos.
uses: Product detail pages with several photos per color and a size picker.
Stores where shoppers need to zoom into fabric, texture, or small print.
avoids: Use lightbox-gallery for a photo grid that opens into a viewer, with no variants.
Use carousel for marketing slides or cards.

items.title: Product listing
items.summary: A storefront grid with price, color and size filters, a sort menu, hover photo swaps, and quick add with a size row.
uses: A shop's collection or category page with a few dozen to a few hundred products.
Catalogs where color and size are the main filters and a quick add saves a trip to the product page.
avoids: One product with many options; use product-detail or product-configurator.
Huge catalogs with faceted server search; keep the card and filter styles but fetch results from your search service.

items.title: Profile page
items.summary: A user profile with cover, bio, stats, activity and project tabs, and an edit sheet that writes back into the page.
uses: A person's own profile with an edit flow
Public creator or member pages inside an app
avoids: Account security or billing settings, use settings-page
A directory of many people, use team-directory

items.title: Progress
items.summary: Show how much of a known task is complete.
uses: Determinate progress for uploads, imports, or long tasks.
Progress with a visible percentage and a check at completion, via showValue.
avoids: Use skeleton while content is loading with no progress to report.
Use usage-meter for quota against a limit, and gauge for dashboard metrics.

items.title: Project board
items.summary: A living workflow board for moving work between stages.
uses: A compact kanban with a handful of tasks across fixed stages.
Boards where moving tasks should be accessible through explicit buttons, not drag only.
avoids: Use reorderable-list when order within one list matters more than stages.
Use timeline for a dated sequence of events.

items.title: Prompt cache
items.summary: An animated explainer for prompt caching: the shared prefix of each request is cached once, later requests read it back, and the cost and time saved add up.
uses: A docs page or blog post that explains why a stable prefix makes repeat requests cheaper and faster.
A pricing or usage page that shows how cache reads, writes and the time to live affect cost.
avoids: Use context-window to show how much of a model's window a conversation fills and when it compacts.
Use token-inspector to show how text splits into tokens and what each costs.

items.title: Prompt studio
items.summary: One card for editing, testing and shipping a prompt template: variables as chips with sample values, a test run against the chosen model, and versions you can compare and promote to production.
uses: A settings or admin page where a support lead or engineer tunes the prompt behind one AI feature and tests it on real cases.
Prompt management that needs a compact version history with authors, a diff against an earlier version and a visible production pointer.
avoids: Use ai-chat for an end user conversation; this card edits templates, not messages.
Use model-arena to compare the replies of several models side by side on one prompt.

items.title: Provider keys
items.summary: A settings card for bring-your-own-key AI products. Each provider row shows its real mark, the masked key, a status and when the key was last used. You can reveal a key for five seconds, copy, rotate or remove it with undo. Adding or rotating a key opens an inline form that checks the format as you type, then tests the connection before saving.
uses: A settings page where users add their own Anthropic, OpenAI, Google AI, Mistral or xAI keys.
Showing which providers are connected, which keys were rejected, and when each key was last used.
avoids: Choosing a model for a request; use model-picker.
Managing your own product's API keys for customers with scopes and expiry; use secret-rotation or a table.

items.title: Provider status
items.summary: A status card for the AI providers your product depends on. Each row shows the provider's real mark, its health as an icon and label, p50 latency and a 30-day uptime bar with a tooltip for each day. An incident row expands into its timeline of updates, and the card checks again on a visible countdown.
uses: Showing the live health, latency and recent uptime of the model providers your product routes to.
Explaining degraded AI features to users or admins with the provider's incident updates in place.
avoids: A full public status page with components, subscriptions and history: build a page, not a card.
A single provider's state inside a chat header: use agent-status or a small badge.

items.title: Race bar chart
items.summary: A ranking over time: bars overtake each other on springs, values count up, and a timeline you can play or scrub.
uses: Showing how the leaders of a ranking change across many periods.
A launch or recap moment where the motion itself is the point.
avoids: Use line-chart when exact trends over time matter more than rank.
Use bar-chart for a single period's comparison.

items.title: Radar chart
items.summary: Two or three profiles on one web: shapes morph when you swap a profile, and a sweep across the axes compares values in place.
uses: Comparing the profile of a few options across shared measures.
Showing strengths and gaps at a glance, such as scores or ratings.
avoids: Use bar-chart when the precise difference on one measure matters.
Use plan-matrix for feature comparisons with yes or no values.

items.title: Radio cards
items.summary: Selectable option cards with a sliding selection ring, price and description slots, and radio keyboard behavior.
uses: Choices where each option needs a description, price, or estimate to decide.
Plan, shipping, region, or size pickers inside checkout and setup flows.
avoids: Use radio-group for short text-only options.
Use segmented-control for two to four view modes that switch content instantly.

items.title: Radio group
items.summary: Choose one option from a visible set.
uses: Two to six mutually exclusive options that need descriptions, such as plans.
Form choices that should submit natively through name.
avoids: Use segmented-control for short inline view options.
Use select for longer lists.

items.title: Range histogram slider
items.summary: A price range over a live histogram of the data, lighting the bars inside the range and settling on bar edges.
uses: Marketplace and search filters for price, size, or distance where the distribution guides the choice.
Analytics filters that trim outliers from a numeric column.
avoids: Use slider for a plain range without data behind it.
Use elastic-slider or slider for a single value.

items.title: Rating
items.summary: A simple, accessible way to capture a numeric opinion.
uses: Collecting a 1 to N score in reviews or feedback forms.
Displaying average scores, with readOnly and allowHalf.
avoids: Use slider for continuous values.
Use reactions for emoji feedback on content.

items.title: Reactions
items.summary: Acknowledge a post in one tap, with counts that roll.
uses: Lightweight acknowledgement on comments, posts, or release notes.
Slack-style reaction pills with counts and a picker for new reactions.
avoids: Use a reply field such as ai-composer when people need to say something specific.
Use action-swap for a single like or follow toggle without counts.

items.title: Realtime stream
items.summary: A live line that scrolls at 60fps as readings arrive, holds still on hover to read, and pops a marker on every anomaly.
uses: Live monitoring panels and status pages.
A hero on an infrastructure or observability page where motion shows the system is alive.
avoids: Use line-chart for static time series.
Use brush-chart for long histories people zoom into.

items.title: Reasoning block
items.summary: The collapsible thinking block of an AI reply. While the model thinks, a shimmering label counts the seconds and the latest reasoning streams underneath. When it finishes, it folds to "Thought for 7s" and opens to show the full reasoning as calm steps with headings.
uses: Showing a reasoning model's thinking above its answer in a chat or agent transcript.
Letting people audit why an assistant reached a recommendation without crowding the reply.
avoids: Tool or function calls with inputs and outputs: use ToolCall.
A multi step agent plan with checkable tasks: use Agent plan.

items.title: Reasoning tree
items.summary: An illustration of tree search over thoughts: candidates are scored, weak branches fade, the best expand, and the winning path from question to answer draws in.
uses: Explainers, docs and landing pages that teach tree of thoughts, beam search or test time search over reasoning steps.
Showing why a wider search can beat a greedy one, with a control the reader can change and replay.
avoids: Use agent-run or research-run to show a real agent's steps and output as they stream.
Use agent-loop to explain the plan, act and observe cycle of a tool using agent.

items.title: Referral card
items.summary: A give-and-get referral card where people copy or share their invite link, invite friends by email as chips, and watch invites move from invited to signed up to earned, with the credit total counting up and a milestone reward unlocking.
uses: A referral or invite program in account settings, billing or an onboarding checklist.
Showing a person what their invites have earned and how close they are to a bonus reward.
avoids: Team member invites with roles and permissions; use a members table.
Public leaderboards or affiliate payouts with many columns; use a table.

items.title: Release readiness
items.summary: A launch checklist that keeps prerequisites, progress, and the final action together.
uses: A pre-launch or handoff gate where several checks must be done before one action unlocks.
Release or launch checklists with a readiness bar and owners.
avoids: Use onboarding-checklist for a user's own getting-started tasks.

items.title: Reorderable list
items.summary: Organize items with direct drag and drop.
uses: Short user-ordered lists such as priorities or a playlist.
Lists that must be reorderable by keyboard as well as by drag.
avoids: Use sortable-data-table when order comes from a column.
Use swipe-actions when rows need quick actions rather than reordering.

items.title: Reply draft
items.summary: An AI email reply drafter where Claude streams a reply under a received Gmail message. Quick replies steer a fresh draft, tone and length rewrite it with a single crossfade, and you can edit the finished draft before you insert it.
uses: Drafting a reply to an email, ticket or message with an AI model, where the reader reviews and edits before sending.
Offering quick reply intents plus tone and length controls for generated text.
avoids: Free-form chat with a model: use a chat or composer component instead.
Inline autocomplete while typing: use ghost-text.

items.title: Research run
items.summary: Deep research that plans searches, reads sources with their marks, and streams a cited answer where every chip lights up the sentence it supports.
uses: An answer engine or deep research feature that searches, reads and cites.
Internal knowledge search where people must verify each claim.
avoids: Open ended conversation without sources; use ai-chat.
An agent that edits files or runs tools; use agent-run.

items.title: Resizable panels
items.summary: Trade space between panes by dragging the divider between them.
uses: Editor, mail, or dashboard layouts where people trade space between side-by-side panes.
Sidebars that should collapse by dragging or flicking toward the edge.
avoids: Use drawer for a panel that slides over the page.
Use tabs when only one pane needs to be visible at a time.

items.title: Response feedback
items.summary: A feedback control for AI replies where thumbs down opens an inline panel with reason chips and an optional note, thumbs up fills and asks what was good, and a submit shows a short thank-you before folding back into the row.
uses: Collecting thumbs up and down on AI replies in a chat, copilot or search answer.
Gathering structured reasons (inaccurate, unsafe) for model evaluation or support triage.
avoids: Star or numeric ratings of a product or session: use rating.
General product feedback not tied to one reply: use feedback-morph.

items.title: Revenue explorer
items.summary: A SaaS revenue chart you zoom with a brush while paths, axes and figures glide to the range.
uses: Monthly MRR or revenue broken into new, expansion, and churn on an analytics page.
Charts where people need to zoom a date range with an overview brush and compare against a prior period.
avoids: Use mrr-waterfall to explain how MRR moved between two points in time.
Use metric-explorer for a row of KPI cards that open into a chart.

items.title: Revenue globe
items.summary: A dotted globe where live payments arc home to headquarters, with a replayable day.
uses: Revenue or operations overviews showing where payments come from right now.
Showcase pages where a live globe with arcs and a day timeline adds impact.
avoids: Use a table or bar-chart when exact regional numbers matter more than the view.
Use customer-galaxy to explore accounts rather than transactions.

items.title: Rich text editor
items.summary: A lightweight editor with markdown shortcuts, a floating toolbar, a slash menu, and HTML and markdown output.
uses: Comments, notes, and posts where people expect markdown shortcuts and a selection toolbar.
Forms that need Markdown or clean HTML out without pulling in a full editor framework.
avoids: Use textarea for plain text, or mention-input when the only rich part is tagging people.
Use inline-edit for a single line edited in place.

items.title: Ridgeline
items.summary: Overlapping distributions, one ridge per group: hover to lift a ridge and read its quartiles, switch datasets and every curve morphs.
uses: Seasonal or categorical distributions such as temperatures by month or response times by region.
Showing where two groups differ in shape, such as bimodal winters.
avoids: Use beeswarm when each individual observation matters.
Use bar-chart when only one summary number per group matters.

items.title: Roles and permissions
items.summary: A permissions matrix with group toggles that ripple, role duplication and a review bar.
uses: Workspace settings where admins edit what each role can do.
Permission matrices with grouped permissions and a review step before saving.
avoids: Use team-members to assign roles to people.
Use switch rows in settings-page for a few on and off settings.

items.title: Ruler slider
items.summary: A tape of ticks that slides under a fixed needle, with momentum, snapping, and a rolling readout.
uses: Onboarding and profile flows that ask for body measurements or goals.
Mobile-first inputs where dragging a scale is easier than typing.
avoids: Use number-field when people know the exact number and prefer to type it.
Use slider or elastic-slider when the value is relative, like volume.

items.title: Sand text
items.summary: A headline made of sand that pours into the letters, crumbles where the cursor digs, and heals itself.
uses: A hero headline or section title that should be fun to touch.
Short words that change on a selection, like a product name or theme.
avoids: Body copy or long headings; use in-view-title or text-reveal.
Text that must stay readable while people interact near it, like form labels.

items.title: Sankey flow
items.summary: Flows between stages as ribbons with drifting particles; hover any node or ribbon to pour its share through the whole journey.
uses: Showing how a total splits and recombines across three to five stages.
Explaining where a funnel leaks, with the share at each step one hover away.
avoids: Use bar-chart for a simple linear funnel with no branches.
Use sunburst for a strict hierarchy where each part has one parent.

items.title: Scroll area
items.summary: A native scroll container with thin overlay scrollbars and edge fades that appear only when content overflows.
uses: Panels, sidebars, and popovers whose content can outgrow their box.
Horizontal strips of cards or chips that need mouse-wheel scrolling and snap points.
avoids: Use carousel when items should page one at a time with controls.
Do not wrap the whole page; let the document scroll natively.

items.title: Scroll story
items.summary: A feature section where scrolling the copy drives a pinned product view through each step.
uses: Marketing pages that walk through a product in a few steps as people scroll.
Feature sections where a pinned product view should change with the copy.
avoids: Use scroll-highlight for a single paragraph that reveals with scroll.
Use chaos-to-order for one before and after switch.

items.title: Scrub input
items.summary: A Figma-style number field: drag the label to scrub, or type values, units, and arithmetic.
uses: Position, size, rotation, and opacity fields in an inspector panel.
Dense settings where typing exact values and dragging both matter.
avoids: Use number-field for a normal form with stepper buttons and a visible label.
Use slider when the range and position matter more than the exact number.

items.title: Search field
items.summary: A recognizable search entry point with clear affordances.
uses: Filtering a visible list or table in place.
Toolbar search where the query should be clearable with one click.
avoids: Use expanding-search for compact header search with results.
Use combobox when the search sets a form value.

items.title: Search results
items.summary: A faceted workspace search page with suggestions, facet counts that follow the query, filter chips, mixed doc, person and file results with highlighted matches, a gliding keyboard cursor and a preview pane.
uses: A full search page for a workspace or knowledge base that returns several kinds of things at once.
Search where people narrow by type, team, and date, and want to read a match before opening it.
avoids: Use command-palette for quick jump to navigation from any screen.
Use product-listing for a storefront grid filtered by price, color, and size.

items.title: Seat manager
items.summary: A team seats and billing card where avatars and a seat meter show members, invites and open seats against what you pay for, a stepper rolls the prorated charge for today and the new monthly total live, and changes go through a confirm step before anyone is charged. Pending invites can be resent or revoked with undo, and when every seat is taken the card says so and offers to add one.
uses: Letting a team admin add or remove paid seats with the price impact visible before paying.
Showing seat usage against purchased seats, including invites that reserve a seat.
avoids: Managing roles and permissions for many members: use a member table and link to this card for seats.
Usage based or credit billing: use credit-topup or a usage meter instead.

items.title: Seat mapNew
items.summary: An event seat picker with a curved concert hall map, price tiers, zoom and pan, sold, held and wheelchair seats, and a live summary with fees and a hold countdown.
uses: Reserved seating for concerts, theatre, sports and conferences where the buyer picks exact seats.
Any spatial picker with priced places: tables in a restaurant plan, desks in an office, cabins on a deck.
avoids: Use a quantity stepper with best available when seats are general admission or assigned by the box office.
Use availability-picker for choosing times rather than places.

items.title: Security settings
items.summary: An account security page with guided two-factor setup, password change and active sessions.
uses: The security tab of account settings with two-factor setup, password change, and sessions.
Guided TOTP setup that walks through scan, verify, and backup codes.
avoids: Use settings-page for general account and workspace settings.
Use api-keys for managing developer tokens.

items.title: Segmented control
items.summary: Switch between a small set of related views.
uses: Two to five short view options like Day, Week, and Month.
Toolbar toggles between layouts or modes that apply immediately.
avoids: Use tabs when each option swaps a panel of content.
Use radio-group in forms or when options need descriptions.

items.title: Select
items.summary: A compact choice field with a keyboard friendly menu.
uses: A short fixed list where typing is not needed, such as region or sort order.
Form fields that should submit natively through Radix's hidden select via name.
avoids: Use combobox for long or searchable lists.
Use multi-select when several values can be chosen.

items.title: Selection toolbar
items.summary: A contextual batch action surface that appears when items are selected.
uses: Bulk actions for checkbox-selectable tables or grids.
Floating bars that appear only while items are selected.
avoids: Use dropdown-menu for per-row actions.

items.title: Semantic zoom
items.summary: An infinite-zoom map of a company that reveals teams, projects, tasks and people as you fly in.
uses: Workspace or portfolio overviews where people zoom from the whole company to one task.
Hierarchical data where each zoom level should show different detail.
avoids: Use tree-view for a plain hierarchy people scan and expand.
Use project-board for working on tasks.

items.title: Settings command
items.summary: Workspace settings where a search field grows into a palette that flies you to any setting.
uses: Workspace or account settings with several sections and many options.
Admin consoles where support links people to a specific setting.
avoids: Use settings-page for a short, paged profile form with a few fields per section.
Use command-palette for app wide navigation and actions, not just settings.

items.title: Settings page
items.summary: Account settings with a gliding section nav and a save bar that morphs in as you edit.
uses: Account or workspace settings with several sections.
Forms that should show a save bar only when something changed.
avoids: Use security-settings for sessions, two factor, and passwords.
Use billing-overview for plan and invoice management.

items.title: Share access
items.summary: A share panel: invite people as validated email chips with suggestions, change roles from a compact menu, remove with undo, switch link access and copy the link, with every change landing in place.
uses: A Share button on a document, board or project that controls who can open it and what they can do.
Inviting teammates by email with suggestions from a workspace directory.
avoids: Use the invite-people block for inviting people to a whole workspace with seats and plans.
Use copy-button alone when there is only a public link to share.

items.title: Share sheet
items.summary: A Share button that opens into a panel with copy link, access level, channels, and people to send to.
uses: A Share button on a document, design, or board header where people share often.
Sharing flows that combine copy link, access level, and sending to a few recent people.
avoids: Use copy-button when all you need is to copy a URL.
Use dialog when sharing needs a full form, such as roles per person or an email search.

items.title: Sheet stack
items.summary: Nested sheets that stack with depth, drag to dismiss, and become stacked dialogs on wide screens.
uses: Mobile settings where each row opens a deeper page and back should feel spatial.
Nested pickers, such as choosing a workspace and then a project inside it.
avoids: Use dialog for a single confirmation or form with no nested steps.
Use bottom-sheet for one sheet with snap points.

items.title: Shortcut recorder
items.summary: Record key combinations into key caps, with conflict warnings, Kbd, and a searchable cheatsheet.
uses: Settings pages where people remap keyboard shortcuts.
A keyboard shortcut cheatsheet or help dialog, with ShortcutList.
avoids: Use ShortcutKbd alone when shortcuts are fixed and only need to be shown.
Use command-palette to let people run actions by name rather than bind keys.

items.title: SidebarPro4
items.summary: App and docs sidebars: a folding rail, a workspace switcher, a mail shell, and a docs tree.

items.title: Sign in
items.summary: A sign in card that morphs from email to a six digit code to your account.

items.title: Signature pad
items.summary: Smooth ink that thins with speed, with undo, replay, and PNG or SVG export.
uses: Contracts, delivery confirmations, and consent forms that need a drawn signature.
Initials or quick sketches where pen pressure and natural stroke width matter.
avoids: Use input for a typed name when a legal drawn signature is not required.
Use file-upload when the user already has a scanned signature image.

items.title: Sign up form
items.summary: An account creation flow with field validation, password strength, and a clear completion state.

items.title: Site footer
items.summary: A website footer with link columns and newsletter, a minimal layout, and a large fading Arc mark.
uses: The closing section of a marketing, docs, or product site.
Footers that need a newsletter signup and a status link.
avoids: Use a plain row with breadcrumb or links inside signed-in app screens.
Use contact-section when the main goal is to start a conversation.

items.title: Site header
items.summary: A sticky website header that turns solid on scroll, with a gliding active link, mega menu panels, and a mobile sheet.
uses: The top bar of a marketing site, landing page, or docs site.
Product sites with grouped destinations that deserve a mega menu with a feature card.
avoids: Use workspace-sidebar or sidebar-rail inside a signed-in app.
Use morph-nav for a single-surface animated navigation with built-in search.

items.title: Skeleton
items.summary: Reserve space while content is still loading.
uses: Loading states for content whose shape is known, like a profile or comment.
Swapping a placeholder into real content with a crossfade and height spring.
avoids: Use progress when you can report a percentage.
Use empty-state when loading finished and there is nothing to show.

items.title: Skeleton morph
items.summary: Loading skeletons that grow into the real content, block by block, instead of swapping.
uses: Profile cards, feeds, and lists that load in under a few seconds.
Dashboards where the layout is known before the data arrives.
avoids: Use skeleton for long lists of hundreds of rows; layout animation there is costly.
Use a progress indicator when loading takes more than a few seconds.

items.title: Slider
items.summary: Pick a value or a range on a track that follows your finger.
uses: Approximate values like volume, opacity, or a price range.
Ranges with two thumbs, labelled marks, and a formatted readout.
avoids: Use number-field when the exact number matters.
Use progress to show a value people cannot change.

items.title: Slope chart
items.summary: Before and after on two axes: lines draw in, rank moves sit beside each value, and switching datasets slides every line to its new slope.
uses: Showing which items rose, which fell, and how the order changed between two periods.
Replacing a grouped bar chart when the change is the story.
avoids: Use line-chart for three or more moments.
Use bar-chart when only the latest values matter.

items.title: Slot text
items.summary: Text and numbers that spin into their new value on staggered slot machine reels.

items.title: Small multiples
items.summary: A trellis of small line charts that reads as one chart, with a synced crosshair, a shared or independent y scale that springs the axes, sorting with a FLIP reorder, a ghost of the overall total behind every panel and dimming for flat trends.
uses: Comparing revenue, signups or usage across regions, products, plans or channels over the same months.
Showing which segments grow, shrink or stall at a glance, with one shared crosshair to read every value for the same period.
avoids: Use line-chart when two or three series need to be read against each other on one plot.
Use metric-explorer or kpi-drilldown when a person picks one metric and drills into its detail.

items.title: Smart form fill
items.summary: A paste-to-fill form card where AI reads an email signature or messy notes and fills a contact field by field. Each value flashes in with a confidence dot, its source lights up in the pasted text, low-confidence guesses ask for review, and Undo puts the old values back.
uses: People paste an email signature, a forwarded message or notes and expect the record to fill itself.
You need visible confidence and an easy review path before AI-filled data is saved.
avoids: Plain data entry with no unstructured source; use form-field and input.
Long multi-page applications; use multi-step-form and add a paste step to one page.

items.title: Smart scheduler
items.summary: A scheduling card where one sentence like "Find 30 min with Maya and Leo next week, mornings" is read into chips. The three best slots are then ranked across everyone's Google Calendar and Outlook calendars, with an availability strip per person and conflicts called out. Picking a slot opens a draft invite with a Google Meet link, ready to send.
uses: A scheduling assistant inside a CRM, recruiting tool, or team app that books internal meetings from one sentence.
Showing why a time was suggested: who is free, what conflicts, and what is tentative.
avoids: Public booking pages where guests pick from your open times; use availability-picker or booking-pill.
Browsing or editing a full calendar; use week-calendar or month-calendar.

items.title: Social proof toast
items.summary: A stack of social proof notifications for landing and pricing pages, where recent trials, upgrades and verified purchases from people and companies arrive every few seconds. The stack pauses and fans out on hover, and visitors can dismiss any toast.
uses: Showing recent trials, purchases or upgrades on a landing or pricing page.
A live activity feed for a launch or waitlist page (people joining, teams upgrading).
avoids: System feedback after a user action (saved, copied, failed): use toast or undo-toast.
Inside a signed in product where activity is not marketing: use an activity feed list.

items.title: Sortable data table
items.summary: Compare structured records with sortable columns.
uses: Tabular records people sort and select, such as projects, invoices, or users.
Tables that need Shift-click range selection and a count line with Clear.
avoids: Use data-grid when people edit cells like a spreadsheet.
Use timeline for chronological activity.

items.title: Source cards
items.summary: A row of cited sources under an AI answer where cards stream in with real site marks while the model searches, the overflow collapses into a stack of favicons, hovering lifts a preview with the passage, and an inline [n] citation highlights its card.
uses: Citations under an AI search or docs assistant answer.
Showing live search progress ("Searching 3 of 8") while an agent browses.
avoids: A full search results page with many results and filters; use a list layout instead.
Tool calls with arguments and outputs; use tool-call.

items.title: Sparkline
items.summary: Show a compact trend beside a value.
uses: A compact trend inside a card, table row, or KPI tile.
Small charts people can scrub by pointer or keyboard to read past values.
avoids: Use bar-chart for comparing discrete periods with axes.
Use stat-card or metric-card when only the latest value matters.

items.title: Speculative decoding
items.summary: An illustration of speculative decoding: a fast draft model guesses a few tokens, the target model checks them in one pass, and accepted guesses join the answer.
uses: Explaining why a product answers faster: docs, model pages, inference dashboards and blog posts about latency.
Showing a recorded speculative run from your own server, with acceptance and tokens per pass for a chosen draft length.
avoids: Use text-stream to show an answer streaming to a user; this card explains the mechanism behind the speed.
Use token-inspector to look at token probabilities and alternatives for one answer.

items.title: Speech player
items.summary: A read-aloud player for AI replies. The Read aloud button in the message's action row turns into a compact player with play, a scrubbable progress bar, speed and a voice picker, and a highlight follows the spoken word through the reply, karaoke style.
uses: A chat or answer surface where people want a reply read out, with the spoken word followed in the text.
Accessibility and hands free reading for long AI answers, summaries or briefings.
avoids: Use dictation-button to turn speech into text in a composer.
Use a plain audio player for podcasts or long recordings without a transcript to highlight.

items.title: Spend alert
items.summary: A budget and spend alert card where the threshold is set right on the live spend bar, with forecast, Email, Slack and PagerDuty toggles, a hard stop and a live preview of the Slack message the alert will post.
uses: Letting a team set a monthly budget and alert threshold for metered spend.
Showing how close current and forecast spend are to an alert line.
avoids: Read-only usage reporting with no settings; use usage-forecast or usage-billing instead.
Per-seat plans with no metered spend.

items.title: Split bar
items.summary: A single 100% bar split into shares: rest on a segment to widen it and read its exact figures, toggle segments from the legend and the rest reflow, with labels inside when they fit and on leader lines when they don't.
uses: A compact part to whole view that fits in a card row or a dashboard header.
Comparing shares where people also want exact figures on demand and the option to leave a category out.
avoids: Use bar-chart to compare absolute values across many categories.
Use donut-chart when the total in the middle is the headline, or waffle-chart for a count of units.

items.title: Split button
items.summary: A primary action with a menu of nearby alternatives.
uses: One default action with a few close variants, like Merge with Squash and Rebase.
Export or share actions where one format is the usual pick and others sit behind the chevron.
avoids: Use dropdown-menu when there is no default action and every option is equal.
Use button when there are no alternatives.

items.title: Spotlight grid
items.summary: A feature grid where light follows the pointer, cards play live demos, and a click morphs a card into its detail.
uses: A product landing page section that shows four features with live, hands-on previews.
Developer tool marketing where a small working demo explains a feature better than copy.
avoids: Use use-case-gallery for a browsable set of customer or use case stories.
Use expandable-card when you need a single card that expands, not a whole feature grid.

items.title: Starter prompts
items.summary: A greeting and a grid of starter cards for the empty state of an AI app. The cards are grouped into Write, Code, Analyze and Plan tabs, and a shuffle swaps them with a short staggered crossfade. Picking a card fills the composer, and cards that use a connected app show its mark (Gmail, GitHub, Notion, Linear, Google Calendar).
uses: The empty state of a chat, copilot or agent, before the first message.
Teaching what an assistant can do with connected tools, such as Gmail, GitHub or Notion.
avoids: Inside a running conversation; use follow-up suggestion chips in the chat thread instead.
A command launcher with search; use command-palette or ai-command.

items.title: Stats band
items.summary: Headline numbers that count up in view, each with a tiny visual that proves it and a context line on hover, plain or in a hairline grid.
uses: Marketing pages that back a claim with a few numbers.
About and investor pages with headline metrics.
avoids: Live product metrics with trends. Use Metric card or Metrics dashboard.
More than four numbers. Split them or use a table.

items.title: Stepper
items.summary: Show where a person is in a multi-step flow and what is done.
uses: Showing position in a strict multi-step flow like checkout or account setup.
Flows where people can jump back to completed steps, via onStepSelect.
avoids: Use multi-step-form when you also want the step content, navigation, and success state.
Use onboarding-checklist for loosely ordered tasks.

items.title: Sticker peel
items.summary: Peel stickers off a surface with a real curl, move them around, and stick them back down.
uses: A personal or team page where people arrange badges, achievements, or brand stickers.
A launch or marketing moment that invites people to play with the product's marks.
avoids: Use reorderable-list or a sortable grid when the order of items carries meaning.
Use note-stack for content people need to read and rearrange.

items.title: Streamgraph
items.summary: Layered streams on a wiggle baseline that morph between ranges, with a layer you can isolate and read week by week.
uses: Showing the changing share of topics, channels, or genres week by week.
Storytelling dashboards where the shape of seasonality and spikes is the point.
avoids: Use line-chart when exact values or comparisons between series matter.
Use bar-chart for a few periods or categories.

items.title: Stretch refresh
items.summary: Pull a feed down and a line stretches to tell you when to let go.
uses: Timelines, inboxes, and activity feeds where new entries arrive at the top.
Panels that should support pull to refresh by touch, mouse drag, and trackpad scroll.
avoids: Use a plain list for static content that never refreshes.
Use pagination for paging through older items.

items.title: Sunburst
items.summary: A hierarchy in rings: click a segment and every arc swings around it as the new centre, with a breadcrumb back and a rolling total.
uses: Drilling into where a total comes from, one level at a time.
Showing the share of each part within its parent and within the whole.
avoids: Use donut-chart for a single level of parts.
Use tree-table when people need to compare exact values across many rows.

items.title: Support conversation
items.summary: A responsive message thread with useful quick replies and live feedback.
uses: A support chat or ticket thread with quick replies and attachments.
Help flows that should show a typing indicator and a resolve toggle.
avoids: Use support-widget for a floating help launcher.
Use ai-composer for a prompt input without a thread.

items.title: Support widget
items.summary: An in-app help launcher that grows into live article search, reading, and a chat with your team.
uses: An in-app help launcher with article search, an article reader, and chat.
SaaS products that want one help entry point mounted near the app root.
avoids: Use support-conversation for a full page support chat.
Use ai-composer for an AI prompt input without help articles.

items.title: Swipe actions
items.summary: Reveal row actions with a swipe, or from the same actions in a menu.
uses: Touch-first triage lists such as mail, notifications, or tasks.
Rows with one or two quick actions per side, like Archive and Mark unread.
avoids: Use context-menu or dropdown-menu for desktop-first tables.
Use reorderable-list when rows need to be dragged vertically.

items.title: Switch
items.summary: A tactile toggle for settings that take effect immediately.
uses: Settings that take effect as soon as they are flipped, like notifications.
Settings lists where each row is one on and off preference.
avoids: Use checkbox when the choice waits for a submit button.
Use segmented-control for a choice between named options.

items.title: Tabs
items.summary: Switch between related content in the same context.
uses: Peer views of the same object, such as Overview, Activity, and Settings.
Panels with different heights, where the container should spring between them.
avoids: Use segmented-control for a compact value toggle not tied to panels.
Use accordion for stacked sections people read in order.

items.title: Tag input
items.summary: Turn short text values into removable tags.
uses: Free-form lists of short values like tags, keywords, or emails.
Fields where people add values by pressing Enter or comma.
avoids: Use multi-select or chip-group when values come from a fixed list.
Use input for a single value.

items.title: Task breakdown
items.summary: A goal input where AI breaks one sentence into a plan: tasks stream in with estimates, owners and dependencies, and a live timeline shows whether the deadline holds. Reorder, edit or regenerate any task, then send the plan to Linear or Jira with progress for each issue and links.
uses: Turning a goal or brief into a scoped project plan inside a PM, CRM or internal tool.
Exporting AI drafted work to Linear or Jira with a review step before anything is created.
avoids: Showing an agent working through steps live; use agent-plan.
A full backlog or board with many projects; use a dedicated table or kanban.

items.title: Team directory
items.summary: Searchable people, team filters, and a focused profile panel.
uses: An internal directory where people search colleagues and copy contact details.
Team pages with department filters and a profile pane.
avoids: Use team-members to manage roles and invitations.
Use team-showcase for a public, image-led team section.

items.title: Team members
items.summary: A members list where typed emails turn into chips and fly into pending invites as seats roll.
uses: The team or workspace settings page of a SaaS app.
Inviting several people at once by typing or pasting emails.
avoids: Use team-directory for a browsable people directory.
Use roles-permissions to define what each role can do.

items.title: Team showcase
items.summary: An image led team introduction with profiles that open in place.
uses: About or company pages that introduce the team with portraits.
Sections that need one of four layouts: gallery, filmstrip, directory, or spotlight.
avoids: Use team-directory for an internal, searchable people list.
Use team-members for managing members and roles.

items.title: Team switcher
items.summary: A workspace switcher like Linear, Vercel or Slack. The trigger shows the current workspace's logo and plan. The menu has search, your role in each workspace and a Cmd+1 to 9 shortcut for each, and lets you create or join a workspace inline. A highlight glides between rows, and switching crossfades the trigger through a short loading state.
uses: Switching between organizations, teams or workspaces in a multi-tenant SaaS app.
An account or project picker that needs search, roles and keyboard shortcuts.
avoids: Picking from a short static list of options in a form: use a select or segmented control.
Global navigation across pages and commands: use the command palette block.

items.title: Studio perspectives
items.summary: Portrait led editorial stories with a focused reading state.
uses: Testimonials or editorial stories where the person's portrait matters.
Landing sections that rotate through a few quotes on demand.
avoids: Use logo-marquee when logos are enough social proof.
Use carousel for many short testimonials.

items.title: Text morph
items.summary: Morph a label into its next state, letter by letter.
uses: Status words that change a few letters at a time, such as Follow and Following.
Custom buttons or badges that need a morphing label without the rest of the button.
avoids: Use word-rotate for a sentence with one cycling word.
Use button or action-swap when you want the morph plus button behaviour.

items.title: Text reveal
items.summary: Reveal a short piece of content with restrained motion.
uses: Above-the-fold hero headlines that animate on page load.
Landing page intros where text must appear on first paint even if scripts are slow.
avoids: Use in-view-title for section titles further down the page.
Use scroll-highlight for a key paragraph that reveals with scroll.

items.title: Text shimmer
items.summary: Show ongoing work with a calm light across the words.
uses: AI thinking or loading labels such as Generating summary.
Short status lines that should show ongoing work and settle when done.
avoids: Use text-stream for the response text itself.
Use skeleton for content placeholders and progress for measurable progress.

items.title: Textarea
items.summary: A multiline field for notes, descriptions, and longer text.
uses: Free-form multi-line text like bios, comments, or feedback.
Fields with a live character count, which rolls its digits in the helper row.
avoids: Use input for single-line values.
Use inline-edit with multiline for a description edited in place on a page.

items.title: Theme switcher
items.summary: Four smooth ways to move between light and dark appearance.
uses: A single light and dark toggle in an app or marketing top bar.
Pages that want to run their own view transition from the button's position.
avoids: Use user-menu when theme choice, including system, belongs inside an account menu.
Use theme-switch-rise for quiet product chrome, or theme-switch-eclipse for a dramatic showcase change.

items.title: Eclipse
items.summary: The next appearance crosses the page like an eclipse.

items.title: Rise
items.summary: The next appearance rises into place.

items.title: Split
items.summary: The next appearance opens from a slim center seam.

items.title: Ticket router
items.summary: A support ticket router where messages from Gmail, Intercom, Slack and Zendesk come in one at a time. An AI classifier labels each one with intent, sentiment and confidence, and the ticket moves into a team lane with an assignee. Low confidence tickets wait in a review lane, and one click there routes them to the suggested team.
uses: Showing how an AI classifier triages inbound support messages into team queues.
A live triage widget in a helpdesk or ops dashboard, with a human review lane for low confidence.
avoids: A full ticket inbox with search and bulk actions; use a table or list layout.
A single tool step in a chat transcript; use tool-call.

items.title: Time dial
items.summary: Spin a dial to pick an hour and see which team cities are at work.
uses: Planning a moment across two to five cities, such as calls, releases, or handovers.
Distributed teams that need to see at a glance who is inside working hours.
avoids: Use time-picker for a single local time.
Use date-picker or calendar when the day matters more than the hour.

items.title: Time picker
items.summary: Choose a time with sensible keyboard behavior.
uses: Picking a time of day at a fixed interval, such as meetings or reminders.
Fields that show 12-hour times but store 24-hour HH:mm values.
avoids: Use date-picker for dates, pairing the two for a timestamp.
Use time-dial for a more tactile, showcase time selection.

items.title: Timeline
items.summary: Follow what happened, newest first, grouped by day.
uses: Project history, audit logs, and deploy streams where recency matters.
Live feeds where new updates slide in at the top.
avoids: Use sortable-data-table when people sort or compare.
Use stepper for progress through fixed steps.

items.title: TL;DR toggle
items.summary: An article card with a Full, Summary and Key points switch and a length slider. Switching streams an AI summary in place of the article as the card's height springs to fit, and each key point links back to the paragraph it came from, which gets scrolled to and highlighted.
uses: Offering a quick summary or key points above or in place of a long article, doc or report.
Letting readers verify AI claims against the source, through key points that link back to paragraphs.
avoids: Open-ended questions about content: use an answer or chat component such as ai-answer.
Short content under a couple of paragraphs, where a summary saves no time.

items.title: Toast
items.summary: Brief confirmation for a completed background action.
uses: A single success confirmation, like Changes saved, controlled with local state.
Demos or small apps that do not need a toast queue.
avoids: Use toast-stack for app-wide notifications with types, actions, updates, and stacking.
Use alert for persistent messages that should stay in the page flow.

items.title: Toast stack
items.summary: Stack short results at the edge until you reach for them.
uses: App-wide notifications for async results, errors, and undo.
Loading toasts that morph into success or error when work finishes.
avoids: Use toast for a single locally controlled confirmation.
Use alert for persistent messages tied to a page.

items.title: Table of contents progress
items.summary: A table of contents that reads along with you: a line bends through the nested headings, fills as you scroll, and carries a marker to the current section, with smooth jumps and a time-left countdown.
uses: A documentation page, guide or blog post long enough that readers jump between sections.
An engineering write up or policy where knowing how much is left helps readers commit to it.
avoids: Use tabs when sections are alternatives rather than parts of one document.
Use scroll-progress-ring for a compact overall progress indicator without navigation.

items.title: Toggle group
items.summary: A row of icon or text toggles, single or multiple: one pressed fill glides between options, or each fades in on its own and neighbours join, as in a formatting toolbar.
uses: Formatting toolbars: bold, italic and underline as multiple, alignment as single.
Compact view options on a canvas, map or editor, such as grid or list, or which layers to show.
avoids: Use segmented-control for switching between views, ranges or tabs of content.
Use checkbox or switch for settings in a form that are saved together.

items.title: Tone tuner
items.summary: A brand voice card where two sliders (formality and detail) and Friendly, Confident and Empathetic chips rewrite a customer reply. Each changed sentence crossfades in place, new words can be highlighted against the original, and Copy takes the current version.
uses: A composer or help desk reply that offers AI tone controls before sending.
Brand voice tooling where marketers compare versions of the same copy.
avoids: Free form AI editing with a prompt box: use a chat or composer instead.
Long documents: the card is sized for a message of a few paragraphs.

items.title: Tool call
items.summary: A tool call row for agent transcripts: the tool's mark and the call in plain words, a live state while it runs, and the input and output a click away, with approval and retry when needed.
uses: Showing what tools an AI agent used inside a chat or agent transcript, with the arguments and results one click away.
Human in the loop actions where a call must be allowed or denied inline before it runs, such as posting a message or writing to a database.
avoids: Use agent-run for a full multi step run with a plan, a timeline and live logs rather than inline rows in a message.
Use agent-approvals for a queue of pending approvals across many agents and runs.

items.title: Tooltip
items.summary: Short supporting text for unfamiliar controls.
uses: One-line labels on icon-only buttons in toolbars.
Revealing the full text of truncated labels on hover or focus.
avoids: Use popover for anything with links or controls inside.
Use hover-card for rich previews such as a person or link.

items.title: Training run
items.summary: A fine-tuning job card where a live train and validation loss curve draws across a fixed step axis that doubles as the epoch progress bar. It shows the learning rate, elapsed time, ETA and the latest evals and checkpoints, has Pause and Cancel while it runs, and ends in results with a Deploy button.
uses: A fine-tuning or training job page in an AI platform, where people watch loss, pause, cancel and deploy.
An eval or distillation run that reports a loss curve, checkpoints and a final score.
avoids: A generic multi-series chart with no job lifecycle: use line-chart.
A short agent task with steps rather than a loss curve: use agent-status.

items.title: Tree table
items.summary: A table with nested rows, tri-state selection, hierarchy-preserving sort, and lazy-loaded children.
uses: File or folder listings with size, owner, and modified columns.
Budgets, org charts, or accounts where totals roll up through nested rows.
avoids: Use tree-view for navigation trees without columns.
Use data-grid or sortable-data-table for flat records.

items.title: Tree view
items.summary: Navigate nested folders and structured content.
uses: Files, folders, and nested categories people expand and select.
Side panels next to code-block or a detail view where selection drives content.
avoids: Use accordion for a few collapsible sections of content.
Use breadcrumb to show the path to the current page.

items.title: Treemap
items.summary: A squarified treemap: click to drill and the tiles grow to fill the view, with a breadcrumb back and metrics that morph every tile.
uses: Many parts where the biggest ones matter and people drill for detail.
Showing size and a second measure at once.
avoids: Use bar-chart when exact comparisons between similar values matter.
Use sunburst when the depth of the hierarchy is the story.

items.title: Trial banner
items.summary: A trial status banner where a ring counts down the days left, the copy names what the workspace loses, and the upgrade path is one click away. It comes as a slim banner, a sidebar card or a header pill. It shifts to a warning tone in the last days, has expired and upgraded states, and folds into the pill when dismissed or snoozed.
uses: A SaaS app with a free trial that needs a quiet, always visible upgrade path.
Telling a workspace what it loses when the trial ends and nudging harder in the last days.
avoids: A hard paywall that blocks a feature; use a modal or an upgrade screen instead.
Generic announcements or release notes; use a plain banner or toast.

items.title: Two-factor setup
items.summary: A two-factor setup card where you scan a real, working authenticator QR code, type the 6-digit code into slots that move to the next box on their own, and save your backup codes before it turns on. Every step shares one fixed-size card, so it moves between steps with a short slide and never changes size.
uses: Turning on authenticator app two-factor from account or workspace security settings.
Enforced two-factor onboarding for admins after sign-in.
avoids: SMS or email one-time codes only: use otp-input in a sign-in form.
Passkeys or WebAuthn enrolment, which needs no QR or code step.

items.title: Typewriter terminal
items.summary: A terminal that types a scripted CLI session with a seeded human cadence, colors the shell syntax, and streams output lines, progress bars and spinners, with a scrubber, play/pause and replay controls.
uses: A landing page hero or install section for a developer tool, SDK, or CLI.
