Docs quick starts that show what each command prints before people run it.
avoids: Use code-block for commands and source that people need to read and copy without waiting.
Use log-stream for real, live output from a running process.

items.title: Undo toast
items.summary: Archive or delete rows with a second chance: the gap closes, a countdown toast merges repeat actions, and Undo or ⌘Z puts every row back exactly where it was.
uses: An inbox, notification list, task list or file list where archiving or deleting should be one click with a way back.
Bulk triage, where people remove several items quickly and one toast should summarise them all.
avoids: Irreversible destruction such as deleting a project or revoking keys; use confirm-popover so the consequence is stated first.
General app notifications that are not tied to removing list items; use toast-stack.

items.title: Upgrade prompt
items.summary: An upgrade nudge for the moment someone hits a limit. It shows a usage meter at 50 of 50 AI credits, a rolling price with a monthly and yearly toggle, three concrete unlocks with real model marks, and Upgrade or Maybe later. Upgrading leads into a success state with the new limits, and the card never changes size between states.
uses: An AI product that hits a usage limit (credits, generations, seats) and needs a tasteful, conversion focused nudge.
A paywall moment inside an app, in a dialog, popover or inline in place of the blocked result.
avoids: Comparing several plans side by side: use a pricing table or plan picker.
Buying prepaid credits without a plan change: use credit-topup.

items.title: Uptime status
items.summary: A status page with 90 day uptime bars, a morphing latency chart and an incident timeline.
uses: A public or internal status page with per-service uptime history.
Pages that combine 90 day uptime strips, response time, and an incident timeline.
avoids: Use activity-heatmap for activity counts rather than availability.
Use timeline for an incident history on its own.

items.title: Usage billing
items.summary: A usage based billing dashboard with a projected spend line, meters against limits, alerts, and an upgrade that morphs into a confirm sheet.
uses: A billing page for usage priced SaaS or infrastructure products.
Admin dashboards where finance needs spend alerts and invoice history in one place.
avoids: Use billing-overview for flat seat based plans without meters.
Use plan-comparison or usage-pricing on a public pricing page.

items.title: Usage forecast
items.summary: A billing period usage chart with a forecast cone and a draggable budget that dates the crossing.
uses: Billing or usage pages that warn customers before they hit a budget.
Metered products that show month to date usage with a forecast range.
avoids: Use usage-meter for a simple progress bar against a limit.
Use usage-pricing to estimate price from usage before buying.

items.title: Usage meter
items.summary: Show what fills an allowance and how close it is to the limit.
uses: Quota against a fixed allowance, such as storage, seats, or API calls.
Billing pages that should show what takes the space and how close the plan is to full.
avoids: Use progress for task completion.
Use bar-chart to compare categories without a limit.

items.title: Usage pricing
items.summary: A pricing calculator that finds your plan as you drag seats and traffic.
uses: Pricing pages for plans priced by seats plus usage.
Calculators that should recommend a plan as people move sliders.
avoids: Use plan-comparison for a side by side table of fixed tiers.
Use usage-forecast to project spend for an existing customer.

items.title: User menu
items.summary: Your account, settings, theme, and sign out behind the avatar. Opens as a bottom sheet on phones.
uses: The single account entry point in an app top bar.
Menus that combine presence status, theme preference, account links, and sign out.
avoids: Use dropdown-menu for generic command lists.
Use theme-switch for a standalone light and dark toggle.

items.title: Vector search
items.summary: Documents drop onto a tilted embedding plane and fold into points that cluster by topic; the index links neighbours, a query is typed, embedded and lowered onto the plane, a signal hops along the graph toward it, and a widening ring lights the nearest documents with connecting lines, similarity scores and a ranked list.
uses: A feature section on semantic search, AI answers, or retrieval over a team's docs.
Docs pages introducing embeddings, nearest neighbour search, or approximate indexes.
avoids: Use search-index to explain keyword search with an inverted index.
Use a real scatter or cluster chart to show an actual embedding projection.

items.title: Voice orb
items.summary: A voice mode orb that listens, thinks, and speaks, with a live transcript and call controls.
uses: A voice mode for an assistant where the user needs to see whether it is listening, thinking, or speaking.
Hands-free or call-like flows that need start, mute, a running clock, and end in one compact control.
avoids: Use voice-recorder when the user records a clip to send or save.
Use chat-thread with text-stream for typed chat where no audio is involved.

items.title: Voice recorder
items.summary: Record with a live waveform, review and scrub, then send the take into the thread.
uses: Voice notes in chats, comments, or field notes where speaking beats typing.
A thread of voice bubbles with playback and scrubbing.
avoids: Use now-playing for music or long-form audio.
Use hold-to-confirm for press-and-hold actions that do not record.

items.title: Waffle chart
items.summary: A ten by ten unit chart where every cell is one percent, and cells fly to their new group when the data changes.
uses: Showing shares of one whole where people should be able to count units.
Comparing the same categories across a few datasets, such as countries or years.
avoids: Use line-chart or streamgraph for how shares change over time.
Use bar-chart when exact comparison of many categories matters more than the whole.

items.title: Wallet card
items.summary: A compact account view with balance, recent activity, and focused money actions.
uses: A personal or business balance summary with quick send, deposit, swap, and buy actions.
Dashboards that pair a balance with a small history chart and recent activity.
avoids: Use billing-overview for subscription billing and invoices.
Use wallet-stack for a stack of payment cards.

items.title: Wallet stack
items.summary: Fan a stack of cards and lift one out to see its activity.
uses: A few payment cards, passes, or memberships where people open one to see its balance and activity.
Fintech or wallet screens that want a physical card metaphor with realistic materials.
avoids: Use card-stack for generic swipeable content that is not a card wallet.
Use a plain list or data-grid for many accounts.

items.title: Webhook tester
items.summary: A developer webhook tester where you pick an event, edit its JSON payload and send a signed test event. You watch it go from signed to sent to 200 OK in 184 ms, then read the response body, headers and exact request, and retry failed deliveries from a recent list.
uses: A developer settings page where customers test a webhook endpoint before going live.
Integration onboarding that asks people to prove their handler returns 2xx and verifies signatures.
avoids: Managing many endpoints, filters and event subscriptions: use the webhooks block and link here for testing one.
A general HTTP client for arbitrary methods and headers: this always sends a signed POST with a JSON body.

items.title: Webhooks
items.summary: A webhooks console with delivery history, a payload inspector and retries that roll the rate.
uses: A developer settings page for webhook endpoints, delivery history, and retries.
Consoles that need a payload and headers inspector next to the delivery list.
avoids: Use api-keys for managing tokens.
Use audit-log for account activity rather than outgoing events.

items.title: Week calendar
items.summary: A week calendar where you drag to create, move, and resize events, with color coded calendars, day and agenda views, and swipes on phones.
uses: Scheduling and planning screens where people create, move and resize time blocks across a week.
Team or personal calendars that need several color coded calendars, all day events and an agenda on phones.
avoids: Use month-calendar for a month overview with events per day.
Use calendar or date-picker to pick a date, and time-picker for a single time.
